dānavendrāya bhuvane yajjagādośanāḥ purā .. 1 ..
2.22.d:
2.106
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
स्नानमन्यत्प्रवक्ष्यामि तवाहं दुरितापहम् ॥
दानवेन्द्राय भुवने यज्जगादोशनाः पुरा ॥ 1 ॥
2.22.m: Puṣkara said: / I shall declare to you another bath that removes misfortune, / which Uśanas formerly spoke in the world to the lord of the Dānavas.

2.22.s:
dhanyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ sarvaśatrukṣayaṃkaram ..
prabhātāyāṃ tu śarvaryāṃ bhāskare'nudite tathā .. 2..
2.22.d:
धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं सर्वशत्रुक्षयंकरम् ॥
प्रभातायां तु शर्वर्यां भास्करेऽनुदिते तथा ॥ 2॥
2.22.m: Conferring wealth, bringing renown, granting long life, causing the destruction of all enemies; / when night has turned into dawn and the sun has not yet risen,

2.22.s:
snāyīta bhārgavaśreṣṭha vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā ..
sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ kumbhamathavāpi mahīmayam .. 3 ..
2.22.d:
स्नायीत भार्गवश्रेष्ठ विधिदृष्टेन कर्मणा ॥
सौवर्णं राजतं कुम्भमथवापि महीमयम् ॥ 3 ॥
2.22.m: one should bathe, O best of the Bhṛgus, according to the rite seen in prescribed rules. / A jar of gold, of silver, or even of clay,

2.22.s:
nādeyaiḥ sāgaraistoyaiḥ kalpayitvā yathāvidhiḥ ..
oṣadhīrvinyasettatra samabhāgāḥ sucūrṇitāḥ .. 4 ..
2.22.d:
नादेयैः सागरैस्तोयैः कल्पयित्वा यथाविधिः ॥
ओषधीर्विन्यसेत्तत्र समभागाः सुचूर्णिताः ॥ 4 ॥
2.22.m: having prepared it according to rule with river waters and ocean waters, / one should place herbs therein in equal parts, well-powdered:

2.22.s:
jayā ca vijayā caiva tathā sūkṣmaphalāni ca ..
prasannamukhabījāni bhāṇḍīrakusumāni ca .. 9 ..

जया च विजया चैव तथा सूक्ष्मफलानि च ॥
प्रसन्नमुखबीजानि भाण्डीरकुसुमानि च ॥ 9 ॥
2.22.m: jayā and vijayā, and likewise small fruits, / seeds of prasannamukha, and bhāṇḍīra flowers,

2.22.s:
kṣīrajāpatranirmālyaṃ devīnissārameva ca ..
kallīvarāṅganā caiva gajendrasya ca mañjarī .. 6 ..
2.22.d:
क्षीरजापत्रनिर्माल्यं देवीनिस्सारमेव च ॥
कल्लीवराङ्गना चैव गजेन्द्रस्य च मञ्जरी ॥ 6 ॥
2.22.m: remnants of milk-tree leaves, and the essence of the goddess, / kallīvarāṅganā, and the flower-cluster of the lord of elephants,

2.22.s:
kṣudrajaṃ karajaṃ caiva dhane dvedve vibhāvarī ..
mahaughaṃ pūrtagaṃ caiva bhuvaṃ yakṣabhuvaṃ tathā .. 7 ..
2.22.d:
क्षुद्रजं करजं चैव धने द्वेद्वे विभावरी ॥
महौघं पूर्तगं चैव भुवं यक्षभुवं तथा ॥ 7 ॥
2.22.m: kṣudraja and karaja, two pairs of night-herbs in wealth, / mahaugha and pūrtaga, and earth and yakṣa-earth,

2.22.s:
śaśāṅkamṛgadarpaṃ ca dānaṃ ca kariṇastathā ..
oṣadhyaḥ kathitāstubhyaṃ dāne mantramataḥ śṛṇu .. 8..
2.22.d:
शशाङ्कमृगदर्पं च दानं च करिणस्तथा ॥
ओषध्यः कथितास्तुभ्यं दाने मन्त्रमतः शृणु ॥ 8॥
2.22.m: musk, and the rut of an elephant. / The herbs have been declared to you; hear now the mantra for the gift.

2.22.s:
( oṃnamo bhagavate rudrāya dhavalapāṇḍuropacitabhasmānuliptagātrāya ..
tadyathā ..
jaya jaya vijayavijaya sarvāñchatrūnamukasya kalahavigrahavivādeṣu bhañjabhañja mathamatha sarvatra pratyakṣikāṃ yo'sau yugāntakāle dadhyakṣatairimāṃ pūjāṃ raudrī mūrtisahastāṃ susattvāṃ rakṣatu jīvikāṃ saṃvartakāgnitulyaśca tripurārtikaraḥ yaḥ sarvadevamayaḥ so'pi tava rakṣatu jīvitaṃ nikhi nikhi nikhi svāhā .. )
evaṃ snātastvanenaiva gātreṇa tilataṇḍulam ..
ghṛtāktaṃ jvalite vahnau juhuyātprayataḥ sadā ..9 ...
2.22.d:
( ओंनमो भगवते रुद्राय धवलपाण्डुरोपचितभस्मानुलिप्तगात्राय ॥
तद्यथा ॥
जय जय विजयविजय सर्वाञ्छत्रूनमुकस्य कलहविग्रहविवादेषु भञ्जभञ्ज मथमथ सर्वत्र प्रत्यक्षिकां योऽसौ युगान्तकाले दध्यक्षतैरिमां पूजां रौद्री मूर्तिसहस्तां सुसत्त्वां रक्षतु जीविकां संवर्तकाग्नितुल्यश्च त्रिपुरार्तिकरः यः सर्वदेवमयः सोऽपि तव रक्षतु जीवितं निखि निखि निखि स्वाहा ॥ )
एवं स्नातस्त्वनेनैव गात्रेण तिलतण्डुलम् ॥
घृताक्तं ज्वलिते वह्नौ जुहुयात्प्रयतः सदा ॥9 ॥।
2.22.m: ("Oṃ, homage to the Blessed Lord Rudra, whose body is smeared with bright white abundant ashes. Namely: Triumph, triumph! Be victorious, be victorious! Smash, smash, crush, crush all the enemies of so-and-so in disputes, fights, and quarrels! Visible everywhere, may he who at the end of the cosmic age [receives] this ferocious worship with curd and unbroken rice protect his livelihood together with his form and good being. And equal to the fire of universal destruction, the tormentor of Tripura, who consists of all the gods—may he also protect your life! Nikhi nikhi nikhi svāhā!") / Having thus bathed, one with restrained senses should always offer into the blazing fire with this same body sesame and rice smeared with ghee.

2.22.s:
tataḥ sampūjanaṃ kuryāddevadevasya śūlinaḥ ..
ghṛtakṣīrābhiṣekeṇa gandhapuṣpaphalākṣataiḥ .. 2.106.10 ...
2.22.d:
ततः सम्पूजनं कुर्याद्देवदेवस्य शूलिनः ॥
घृतक्षीराभिषेकेण गन्धपुष्पफलाक्षतैः ॥ 2.106.10 ॥।
2.22.m: Then he should perform the worship of the trident-bearing God of gods / with an anointing of ghee and milk, and with fragrant unguents, flowers, fruits, and unbroken rice,

2.22.s:
dīpadhūpanamaskāraistathā vānnena bhūriṇā ..
gītavādyaiḥ sumadhurairbrāhmaṇānsvastivācanaiḥ .. 11 ..
2.22.d:
दीपधूपनमस्कारैस्तथा वान्नेन भूरिणा ॥
गीतवाद्यैः सुमधुरैर्ब्राह्मणान्स्वस्तिवाचनैः ॥ 11 ॥
2.22.m: with lamps, incense, and prostrations, as well as with abundant food, / with sweet songs and instrumental music, and through brahmins reciting blessings.

2.22.s:
māheśvarasnānamidaṃ hi kṛtvā rakṣohaṇaṃ śatrunibarhaṇaṃ ca ..
kāmānavāpnoti narastu sarvānyānrāma kāṃścinmanasecchatīti .. 12 ..
2.107
puṣkara uvāca ..
snānānyanyāni te vacmi nibodha gadato mama ..
rakṣoghnāni yaśasyāni maṅgalyāni viśeṣataḥ .. 1 ..
snānaṃ ghṛtena kathitaṃ cāyuṣo vardhanaṃ param ..
rāma gośakṛtā snānaṃ paraṃ lakṣmīvivardhanam .. 2 ..
snānaṃ ca kathitaṃ dadhnā paraṃ lakṣmīvivardhanam..
tathā darbhodakasnānaṃ sarvapāpanibarhaṇam .. 3..
palāśabilva kamalakuśasnānaṃ puro hitam ..
vacā haridrā mañjiṣṭhā tagaraṃ cārakaṃ tathā .. 4..
snānametadvinirdiṣṭaṃ rakṣoghnaṃ pāpasūdanam ..
vacāharidrayā yuktaṃ snānaṃ rakṣohaṇaṃ param .. 5 ..
āyuṣyaṃ ca yaśasyaṃ ca dhanyaṃ medhāvivardhanam ..
snānaṃ pavitraṃ maṅgalyaṃ tathā kāñcanavāriṇā .. 6 ...
2.22.d:
माहेश्वरस्नानमिदं हि कृत्वा रक्षोहणं शत्रुनिबर्हणं च ॥
कामानवाप्नोति नरस्तु सर्वान्यान्राम कांश्चिन्मनसेच्छतीति ॥ 12 ॥
2.107
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
स्नानान्यन्यानि ते वच्मि निबोध गदतो मम ॥
रक्षोघ्नानि यशस्यानि मङ्गल्यानि विशेषतः ॥ 1 ॥
स्नानं घृतेन कथितं चायुषो वर्धनं परम् ॥
राम गोशकृता स्नानं परं लक्ष्मीविवर्धनम् ॥ 2 ॥
स्नानं च कथितं दध्ना परं लक्ष्मीविवर्धनम्॥
तथा दर्भोदकस्नानं सर्वपापनिबर्हणम् ॥ 3॥
पलाशबिल्व कमलकुशस्नानं पुरो हितम् ॥
वचा हरिद्रा मञ्जिष्ठा तगरं चारकं तथा ॥ 4॥
स्नानमेतद्विनिर्दिष्टं रक्षोघ्नं पापसूदनम् ॥
वचाहरिद्रया युक्तं स्नानं रक्षोहणं परम् ॥ 5 ॥
आयुष्यं च यशस्यं च धन्यं मेधाविवर्धनम् ॥
स्नानं पवित्रं मङ्गल्यं तथा काञ्चनवारिणा ॥ 6 ॥।
2.22.m:
For having performed this bath sacred to Maheśvara, which destroys demons and eradicates enemies, / a man attains all desires whatever his mind wishes for, O Rāma.
2.107 / Puṣkara said: / I shall tell you of other baths; listen as I speak, / which are particularly destructive of demons, bring renown, and are auspicious.
A bath with ghee is declared to be the highest prolonger of life; / a bath with cow dung, O Rāma, is supreme for increasing prosperity.
And a bath with curd is declared to be supreme for increasing prosperity; / likewise, a bath with water infused with darbha grass destroys all sins.
A bath with palāśa, bilva, lotus, and kuśa is beneficial, [performed] facing eastward; / sweet flag, turmeric, madder, tagara, and cāraka—
this bath is prescribed as slaying demons and eliminating sins. / A bath combined with sweet flag and turmeric is supreme for slaying demons.
It grants longevity, brings renown, brings fortune, and increases intellect; / such is the pure, auspicious bath with water [infused with] gold.

2.22.s:
kramādūnatare kiñcidrūpyatāmrodakaistataḥ ..
tathā ratnodakasnānaṃ saṅgrāmavijayāvaham .. 7 ..
vaiḍūryaṃ madhyataḥ kṛtvā pravālaiḥ parivārayet ..
tena pātreṇa yatsnānaṃ sarvakāmakaraṃ hitam .. 8 ..
snānaṃ sarvauṣadhairmukhyaṃ vivāde vijayapradam ..
sarvagandhodakasnānaṃ saubhāgyārogyakārakam .. 9 ..
tathā bījodakasnānaṃ sarvakarmaprasādhakam ..
tathaivāmalakasnānamalakṣmīnāśanaṃ param .. 2.107.10 ..
tilasiddhārthakaiḥ snānamamaṅgalyapraṇāśanam ..
kevalairvā tilaiḥ snānamathavā gaurasarṣapaiḥ .. 11 ..
snānaṃ priyaṅgunā proktaṃ tathā saubhāgyavardhanam ..
saubhāgyakaṃ tathā snānaṃ nāgakāntāpriyaṅgubhiḥ .. 12 ..
2.22.d:
क्रमादूनतरे किञ्चिद्रूप्यताम्रोदकैस्ततः ॥
तथा रत्नोदकस्नानं सङ्ग्रामविजयावहम् ॥ 7 ॥
वैडूर्यं मध्यतः कृत्वा प्रवालैः परिवारयेत् ॥
तेन पात्रेण यत्स्नानं सर्वकामकरं हितम् ॥ 8 ॥
स्नानं सर्वौषधैर्मुख्यं विवादे विजयप्रदम् ॥
सर्वगन्धोदकस्नानं सौभाग्यारोग्यकारकम् ॥ 9 ॥
तथा बीजोदकस्नानं सर्वकर्मप्रसाधकम् ॥
तथैवामलकस्नानमलक्ष्मीनाशनं परम् ॥ 2.107.10 ॥
तिलसिद्धार्थकैः स्नानममङ्गल्यप्रणाशनम् ॥
केवलैर्वा तिलैः स्नानमथवा गौरसर्षपैः ॥ 11 ॥
स्नानं प्रियङ्गुना प्रोक्तं तथा सौभाग्यवर्धनम् ॥
सौभाग्यकं तथा स्नानं नागकान्ताप्रियङ्गुभिः ॥ 12 ॥
2.22.m:
Then, progressively slightly inferior, with silver water and copper water; / likewise, a bath with water [infused with] gems brings victory in battle.
Having placed a cat's-eye gem in the centre, one should surround it with corals; / the bath [taken] with that vessel fulfills all desires and is beneficial.
A bath with all medicinal herbs is foremost, granting victory in a dispute; / a bath with water [infused with] all perfumes brings good fortune and health.
Likewise, a bath with water [infused with] seeds accomplishes all undertakings; / and in the same way, a bath with myrobalan is supreme for destroying misfortune.
A bath with sesame and white mustard seeds destroys inauspiciousness, / or a bath with sesame alone, or with white mustard seeds.
A bath with priyaṅgu is declared to increase good fortune; / likewise, an auspicious bath [is taken] with nāgakāntā and priyaṅgu.

2.22.s:
purocārukakuṣṭhaiśca tathaiva ca vinirdiśet ..
dhātrīphalena padmaiśca tathāmalakavāriṇā .. 13 ..
2.22.d:
पुरोचारुककुष्ठैश्च तथैव च विनिर्दिशेत् ॥
धात्रीफलेन पद्मैश्च तथामलकवारिणा ॥ 13 ॥
2.22.m: And in the very same way one should prescribe [a bath] with purocāruka and kuṣṭha; / with myrobalan fruit, lotuses, and water with myrobalan,

2.22.s:
lakṣmīvṛddhikaraṃ snānaṃ kathitaṃ bhārgavottama ..
padmotpalakadambaiśca tathā lakṣmīvivardhanam .. 14 ..
2.22.d:
लक्ष्मीवृद्धिकरं स्नानं कथितं भार्गवोत्तम ॥
पद्मोत्पलकदम्बैश्च तथा लक्ष्मीविवर्धनम् ॥ 14 ॥
2.22.m: a bath that causes the increase of prosperity is described, O foremost of the Bhṛgus; / and with lotuses, blue water lilies, and kadamba blossoms it likewise increases prosperity.

2.22.s:
balāmatibalāṃ caiva tathā nāgabalāmapi ..
balāṃ moṭāṃ caturthī tu snānaṃ vai balavardhanam .. 15 ..
2.22.d:
बलामतिबलां चैव तथा नागबलामपि ॥
बलां मोटां चतुर्थी तु स्नानं वै बलवर्धनम् ॥ 15 ॥
2.22.m: Balā, atibalā, and also nāgabalā, / and balā-moṭā as the fourth: a bath [with these] indeed increases strength.

2.22.s:
brahmākarkoṭakīmūlaṃ kumārī padmacāriṇī ..
snāne rogavināśāya smṛtāḥ pratyekaśo dvija .. 16 ..
2.22.d:
ब्रह्माकर्कोटकीमूलं कुमारी पद्मचारिणी ॥
स्नाने रोगविनाशाय स्मृताः प्रत्येकशो द्विज ॥ 16 ॥
2.22.m: Brahmā, karkoṭakī root, kumārī, and padmacāriṇī / are remembered for destroying diseases in bathing, each on its own, O twice-born.

2.22.s:
māṃsīmurācorakanāgapuṣpaiḥ sanāgadānairatināśakāri ..
turuṣkakakkolakajātipūgaiḥ phalaiḥ samastaiḥ sutarāṃ pradadyāt .. 17 ..
2.108
rāma uvāca ..
snānānāmiha sarveṣāṃ yatsnānamatiricyate ..
tanmamācakṣva sakalaṃ sarvakalmaṣanāśanam ..1..
puṣkara uvāca ..
śṛṇu pādodakasnānaṃ sarvakilbiṣanāśanam ..
śravaṇarkṣaṃ vinā hyetadbhavatyardhaphalaṃ yataḥ .. 2 ..
tataḥ kāryaṃ prayatnena śravaṇarkṣe viśeṣataḥ ..
athottarāsu ṣāḍhāsu nirāhāro jitendriyaḥ .. 3 ..
sarvauṣadhaiḥ sarvagandhairdevadevasya cakriṇaḥ ..
pādaṃ pralepayedvidvānkrameṇa caturātmanaḥ .. 4 ..
tatastu kalaśānkuryāccaturaḥ sudṛḍhānnavān ..
sauvarṇānrājatāntāmrānatha vāpi mahīmayān.. 5 ..
tato'niruddhacaraṇau kṛpādbhiḥ kṣālayettataḥ ..
tābhistu kalaśaṃ pūrṇaṃ sthāpanīyaṃ tadagrataḥ .. 6 ..
2.22.d:
मांसीमुराचोरकनागपुष्पैः सनागदानैरतिनाशकारि ॥
तुरुष्ककक्कोलकजातिपूगैः फलैः समस्तैः सुतरां प्रदद्यात् ॥ 17 ॥
2.108
राम उवाच ॥
स्नानानामिह सर्वेषां यत्स्नानमतिरिच्यते ॥
तन्ममाचक्ष्व सकलं सर्वकल्मषनाशनम् ॥1॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
शृणु पादोदकस्नानं सर्वकिल्बिषनाशनम् ॥
श्रवणर्क्षं विना ह्येतद्भवत्यर्धफलं यतः ॥ 2 ॥
ततः कार्यं प्रयत्नेन श्रवणर्क्षे विशेषतः ॥
अथोत्तरासु षाढासु निराहारो जितेन्द्रियः ॥ 3 ॥
सर्वौषधैः सर्वगन्धैर्देवदेवस्य चक्रिणः ॥
पादं प्रलेपयेद्विद्वान्क्रमेण चतुरात्मनः ॥ 4 ॥
ततस्तु कलशान्कुर्याच्चतुरः सुदृढान्नवान् ॥
सौवर्णान्राजतान्ताम्रानथ वापि महीमयान्॥ 5 ॥
ततोऽनिरुद्धचरणौ कृपाद्भिः क्षालयेत्ततः ॥
ताभिस्तु कलशं पूर्णं स्थापनीयं तदग्रतः ॥ 6 ॥
2.22.m:
With spikenard, murā, coraka, and nāgapuṣpa, together with nāgadāna, it destroys distress; / with turuṣka, kakkola, nutmeg, and betel nut, with all these fruits, he should thoroughly administer [the bath].
2.108 / Rāma said: / Among all baths here, that bath which surpasses [all others]— / tell me all about that, which destroys all impurities.
Puṣkara said: / Hear of the bath with the water from [the Lord's] feet, which destroys all sins; / for without the asterism Śravaṇa, this yields only half its fruit.
Therefore, it should be undertaken with effort, especially under the asterism Śravaṇa, / or under Uttarāṣāḍhā, fasting and with senses conquered.
With all medicinal herbs and all perfumes, the wise man should smear the feet / of the God of gods who holds the discus, the Fourfold-formed, in succession.
Then he should prepare four firm, new water-jars / made of gold, silver, copper, or indeed of clay.
Then he should wash the two feet of Aniruddha with well water; / the jar filled with that [water] is to be placed before him.

2.22.m:
Then the two feet of Pradyumna are to be washed with water from a cascade; / and that jar, filled, should be placed before him.
The two feet of Saṃkarṣaṇa are to be washed with lake waters; / and the jar filled with them should be placed before him.
The wise man should wash the two feet of Vāsudeva with river waters; / and the jar filled with them is to be placed before him.
Then worship of the Fourfold-formed [Lord] is to be performed as prescribed; / and he should worship those water-jars with perfumes, garlands, fruits, and unbroken rice.
Then, when the second day arrives, having bathed, having fasted previously, / facing Aniruddha, he should be bathed [with water from the jar] …
and of the god Pradyumna, then of Saṃkarṣaṇa, / and then of Vāsudeva, as of Rāma, the discus-bearer.
(Consecration of all the bells is to be performed / with purifying mantras by the pure Sāttvata, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.

Now I shall tell you the mantras over the four jars,) / auspicious, renown-bringing, and destroying all sins:
"Whose path is unobstructed everywhere and completely undefeated, / whose form is wind, whose self is inconceivable—that Aniruddha is the Lord himself.
With the divine water from his feet, which is auspicious and destroys sin, / taking away sin quickly in this manner, may the Lord increase what is auspicious.
Pradyumna, who illuminates the worlds, possessing the splendour of the sun, / who is the fire that consumes oblations, full of fiery energy—may he bring about my auspiciousness.

राम उवाच ॥
मणीनामथ काम्यानां श्रोतुमिच्छाम्यहं विधिम् ॥
सर्वकामकरं मुख्यं तथा च दुरितापहम् ॥ 1 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
आथर्वणेन विधिना मणिकर्म निबोध मे ॥
ध्रुवस्तिष्ठेत्यृचा वृक्षं प्रत्यक्षमनुमन्त्रयेत् ॥ 2 ॥

सर्वत्र तु मणीनां च निर्माणं केवलं भवेत् ॥

2.22.m:
This bath in the water from the feet of Puruṣottama has been taught as possessing unfailing efficacy. / Following the bath, O you of fierce speed in battle, what more shall I tell you, O Rāma?
2.109 / Rāma said: / Now I wish to hear the procedure for optional amulets, / which fulfills all desires, is supreme, and likewise removes misfortune.
Puṣkara said: / Learn from me the operation of the amulet according to the Atharvanic rule. / One should address the tree visibly with the verse: “Stand firm.”
With the second [verse] minus a quarter-verse, one should sprinkle the site of the amulet; / then with the subsequent quarter of this [verse], one should fashion the amulet.
With the verse “With a kinsman,” one should cut it from that [tree], so says the revelation; / from that hymn, with the third [verse], one should take the amulet.
Everywhere the fashioning of the amulets should be pure; / and the substances suitable for use are declared to be only [proper] seeds.
They should be made the size of a thumb-joint all around; / one should properly produce four knots on them.

अग्रतो मूलतो वापि कल्पमानेऽतिरिच्यते ॥
अरातीयोरित्यनया छिन्द्याच्छस्त्रेण तत्त्ववित् ॥ 7 ॥
अर्थं च सुशिरः कृत्वा ततः प्रक्षाल्य वारिणा ॥

यत्राचक्रुरित्यनया ससूत्रमत उत्तरम् ॥
कुर्यात्तदग्निकुण्डं च प्रबोध्य जुहुयाद् घृतम् ॥ 9 ॥
प्रत्यृचा स्वेन मन्त्रेण सम्पातानयनं भवेत् ॥
कृतशान्त्युदके पात्रे रम्ये लोहमये दृढे ॥ 2.109.10 ॥
स्वलिङ्गोद्धृमन्त्रेण दर्विदण्डादतः परम् ॥
विमुच्य सर्वं तेनैव मन्त्रेण भ्रामयेन्मणिम् ॥ 11 ॥
पात्रे तस्मिंस्ततस्तस्मादुद्धृत्या बन्धनं भवेत् ॥
सकलेनैव मन्त्रेण मन्त्रयेच्च तथोद्गतम् ॥ 12 ॥
सामान्यमिदमुक्तं ते शृणु वैशेषिकं द्विज ॥
अभीवर्तमणौ कर्म तव वक्ष्याम्यतः परम् ॥ 13 ॥
2.22.m:
If while shaping it anything is left over at the tip or at the base, / the knower of truth should cut it off with an instrument using the [verse]: “Those who are hostile.”
And making it properly hollow, then washing it with water, / having placed that vessel in the fire duly according to rule,
with the [verse] “Where they made,” along with a thread thereafter, / one should kindle that fire-pit and offer ghee.
With each verse and with its own mantra, the collecting of consecrated drops should take place / in a lovely, firm vessel made of iron, in which propitiatory water has been prepared.
With the mantra containing its own characteristic mark, taken out from the handle of the ladle after that, / freeing everything, one should rotate the amulet with that very mantra.
Then, having taken it out from that vessel, the fastening takes place; / and one should consecrate it when it has emerged with the complete mantra.
This has been spoken to you as the general [rule]; listen to the specific one, O twice-born. / Hereafter I shall tell you the rite for the Abhīvarta amulet.

2.22.s:
abhīvarttena maṇinetyādyābhistisṛbhirmaṇau ..
atrāyaṃ vāsavaṃ pātraṃ dvebhyaśca pratyṛcaṃ punaḥ 14 ..
dattvā sarveṇa sūktena maṇerādhanvanaṃ bhavet ..
abhīvartamaṇiḥ prokto no vā kāṣṭhānbhṛgūttama .. 15 ..
ayaṃ yonirata iti tasya homo vidhīyate ..
śaśakeṣviha ye śrāntavatsabhaiṣajyabhājanama .. 16 ..
kṣudreṣu yadapāmārgaṃ maṇiḥ śāntavisaṃjñakaḥ ..
ityete yāvaduktāḥ syurvivāhamadhurāśca ye .. 17 ..
pūrvoktena bhaveddharma eteṣāmiti me matiḥ ..
dravyauṣadhimaṇīnāṃ ca sabhāryāṇāṃ tathaiva ca .. 18 ..
dākṣāyaṇamaṇīnāṃ ca bhaveddhomādhiko vidhiḥ ..
oṣadhīnāmihedānīṃ vidhānaṃ śṛṇu bhārgava .. 19 ..
vrīhīṇāṃ vā yavānāṃ vā mūle tu paritaḥ kiret ..
yadi saumya sumantreṇa phalakānyekaviṃśatiḥ .. 2.109.20 ..
2.22.d:
अभीवर्त्तेन मणिनेत्याद्याभिस्तिसृभिर्मणौ ॥
अत्रायं वासवं पात्रं द्वेभ्यश्च प्रत्यृचं पुनः 14 ॥
दत्त्वा सर्वेण सूक्तेन मणेराधन्वनं भवेत् ॥
अभीवर्तमणिः प्रोक्तो नो वा काष्ठान्भृगूत्तम ॥ 15 ॥
अयं योनिरत इति तस्य होमो विधीयते ॥
शशकेष्विह ये श्रान्तवत्सभैषज्यभाजनम ॥ 16 ॥
क्षुद्रेषु यदपामार्गं मणिः शान्तविसंज्ञकः ॥
इत्येते यावदुक्ताः स्युर्विवाहमधुराश्च ये ॥ 17 ॥
पूर्वोक्तेन भवेद्धर्म एतेषामिति मे मतिः ॥
द्रव्यौषधिमणीनां च सभार्याणां तथैव च ॥ 18 ॥
दाक्षायणमणीनां च भवेद्धोमाधिको विधिः ॥
ओषधीनामिहेदानीं विधानं शृणु भार्गव ॥ 19 ॥
व्रीहीणां वा यवानां वा मूले तु परितः किरेत् ॥
यदि सौम्य सुमन्त्रेण फलकान्येकविंशतिः ॥ 2.109.20 ॥
2.22.m:
With the three beginning with “With the victorious amulet,” [one should act] upon the amulet; / here [there is] a vessel for Indra, and again with each verse for the two,
having offered, the fastening of the amulet should be done with the entire hymn. / The Abhīvarta amulet has been declared, or from wood, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
The fire oblation for it is prescribed with “This is the womb from which…” / Among rabbits, here, those which are a vessel of medicine for weary calves,
what is Apāmārga among small [creatures], the amulet called Śāntavi— / as many as these are spoken of, and those which are sweet for marriage,
their procedure should be according to what was said previously; such is my opinion, / for amulets made of substances and herbs, and likewise for married couples.
And for Dākṣāyaṇa amulets there should be an additional rule regarding the fire oblation. / Now hear the procedure for herbs here, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
At the root of rice plants or of barley plants, one should scatter around / twenty-one boards with the auspicious mantra, if it is gentle.

2.22.s:
amuṣminsthānarūḍhāsu yathābhilaṣitāṃ budhaḥ ..
yojayennāma sambhūtāmamukasya vibhūtaye .. 21 ..
ghṛtāhuteti ca dvābhyāṃ ghṛtena prokṣayettataḥ ..
mā te riṣasītyanayā hyā tvā tamabhimantrayet .. 22 ..
gandhaṃ saṃchādayeccaiva tato bhūmetyanantaram ..
ityauṣadhīnāṃ sarvāsāṃ sāmānyo'yaṃ vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ .. 23 ..
ekakādyāstu maṇayaḥ saliṅgaṃ nikhanedbudhaḥ ..
mantreṇa tānpravakṣyāmi yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ .. 24 ..
ekāṅka ekakāmāyetyekāṃke vidhivatkhanet ..
ākrandayati sūktena pradadhnāṃ yadyathāvidhi .. 25 ..
iyaṃ vīrudityanayā vidhivanmadhughaḥ khanet ..
sūktena sukalenāsya maṇerābandhanaṃ bhavet .. 26 ..
imāṃ khanāmītyanayā nitanīliṅgayā khanim ..
pratīcī saumamasitāṃ badhnīyāttu yathāvidhi .. 27 ..
2.22.d:
अमुष्मिन्स्थानरूढासु यथाभिलषितां बुधः ॥
योजयेन्नाम सम्भूताममुकस्य विभूतये ॥ 21 ॥
घृताहुतेति च द्वाभ्यां घृतेन प्रोक्षयेत्ततः ॥
मा ते रिषसीत्यनया ह्या त्वा तमभिमन्त्रयेत् ॥ 22 ॥
गन्धं संछादयेच्चैव ततो भूमेत्यनन्तरम् ॥
इत्यौषधीनां सर्वासां सामान्योऽयं विधिः स्मृतः ॥ 23 ॥
एककाद्यास्तु मणयः सलिङ्गं निखनेद्बुधः ॥
मन्त्रेण तान्प्रवक्ष्यामि यथावदनुपूर्वशः ॥ 24 ॥
एकाङ्क एककामायेत्येकांके विधिवत्खनेत् ॥
आक्रन्दयति सूक्तेन प्रदध्नां यद्यथाविधि ॥ 25 ॥
इयं वीरुदित्यनया विधिवन्मधुघः खनेत् ॥
सूक्तेन सुकलेनास्य मणेराबन्धनं भवेत् ॥ 26 ॥
इमां खनामीत्यनया नितनीलिङ्गया खनिम् ॥
प्रतीची सौममसितां बध्नीयात्तु यथाविधि ॥ 27 ॥
2.22.m:
Among those grown in that place, the wise one should take the desired one, / naming the one that has arisen for the prosperity of so-and-so.
And with the two [verses beginning with] “Offered with ghee,” one should then sprinkle it with ghee; / and one should consecrate it with the [verse] “May you not come to harm,” [saying] “Hither to you…”
And one should conceal its fragrance, and then immediately thereafter with [the hymn] “Earth…” / This is remembered as the general procedure for all herbs.
A wise man should dig up the amulets such as Ekakā with the [verse] bearing the characteristic mark; / I shall declare them properly in due order along with the mantra.
With “O Ekāṅka, for one desire,” one should dig duly for the Ekāṅka [amulet]; / with the hymn “He causes to cry out,” one should offer curds duly.
With the [verse] “This plant,” one should dig duly for the Madhugha [plant]; / with the complete hymn, the fastening of this amulet should be performed.
One should make the excavation with the [verse] “I dig this up,” containing the characteristic mark of the Nitanī; / and one should duly bind the dark [plant] that faces west and belongs to Soma.

2.22.s:
yātvā gandharva indrābhyāṃ kapikacchuṃ khanedvadhaḥ ..
sūktenānena tanmeḍhre prabadhnīyāditi sthitaḥ .. 28 ..
imāṃ khanāmītyanayā daśadhāsrutayā khanet ..
pāṭhāsūktena badhnīyādekā rājñīmiti śrutiḥ .. 29 ..
daśaśīrṣa iti dvābhyāṃ mahākhyaṃ vidhivatkhanet ..
āpaḥ punantvityanena badhnīyāttāṃ yathāvidhi .. 2.109.30 ..
2.22.d:
यात्वा गन्धर्व इन्द्राभ्यां कपिकच्छुं खनेद्वधः ॥
सूक्तेनानेन तन्मेढ्रे प्रबध्नीयादिति स्थितः ॥ 28 ॥
इमां खनामीत्यनया दशधास्रुतया खनेत् ॥
पाठासूक्तेन बध्नीयादेका राज्ञीमिति श्रुतिः ॥ 29 ॥
दशशीर्ष इति द्वाभ्यां महाख्यं विधिवत्खनेत् ॥
आपः पुनन्त्वित्यनेन बध्नीयात्तां यथाविधि ॥ 2.109.30 ॥
2.22.m:
With [the mantra] "Yātvā gandharva indrābhyām", one should dig up cowhage downwards. / With this hymn, standing, he should tie it on his penis.
With [the mantra] "Imāṃ khanāmi", he should dig [it] flowing tenfold. / With the Pāṭhā hymn he should tie it; "one is queen", so says the scripture.
With the two [verses beginning] "Daśaśīrṣaḥ", he should duly dig up the [herb] called Mahā. / With "Āpaḥ punantu", he should duly tie it.

2.22.s:
imāṃ khanāmyauṣadhīṃ tvāṃ ḍhabīṃ nāma tathotkhanet ..
kāṇḍīyāṛktayā tvete badhnīyāttu yathāvidhi .. 31 ..
2.22.d:
इमां खनाम्यौषधीं त्वां ढबीं नाम तथोत्खनेत् ॥
काण्डीयाऋक्तया त्वेते बध्नीयात्तु यथाविधि ॥ 31 ॥
2.22.m: With "Imāṃ khanāmy oṣadhīm", he should likewise dig up the [herb] named Ḍhabī. / With the verse relating to Kāṇḍa, he should duly tie these.

2.22.s:
ya ātmajā ityanayā khanyāditi tathaiva tām ..
anenaiva prabadhnīyādvidvānsūktena taṃ maṇim .. 32 ..
2.22.d:
य आत्मजा इत्यनया खन्यादिति तथैव ताम् ॥
अनेनैव प्रबध्नीयाद्विद्वान्सूक्तेन तं मणिम् ॥ 32 ॥
2.22.m: With "Ya ātmajāḥ", he should likewise dig that up. / With this very hymn, the wise man should bind that amulet.

2.22.s:
ariṣṭastvā khanatu vai pippalaṃ tu khanettathā ..
yāvaddyauriti sūktena tasya cābandhanaṃ bhavet .. 33 ..
2.22.d:
अरिष्टस्त्वा खनतु वै पिप्पलं तु खनेत्तथा ॥
यावद्द्यौरिति सूक्तेन तस्य चाबन्धनं भवेत् ॥ 33 ॥
2.22.m: With "Ariṣṭas tvā khanatu vai", he should dig up Pippala. / With the hymn "Yāvad dyauḥ", its binding should take place.

2.22.s:
sāhasīnāvacetyevaṃ saidhakaṃ ca tathā khanet ..
anevaiva prabadhnīyātsūtreṇa tu yathāvidhi .. 34 ..
2.22.d:
साहसीनावचेत्येवं सैधकं च तथा खनेत् ॥
अनेवैव प्रबध्नीयात्सूत्रेण तु यथाविधि ॥ 34 ॥
2.22.m: With "Sāhasīnāvaca", he should likewise dig up Saidhaka. / With this very [hymn], he should duly tie it with a cord.

2.22.s:
payo'sītyathavā hanyātsvargapatrīṃ yathāvidhi ..
sūktena tāṃ prabadhnīyādanenaiva yathākramam .. 35 ..
2.22.d:
पयोऽसीत्यथवा हन्यात्स्वर्गपत्रीं यथाविधि ॥
सूक्तेन तां प्रबध्नीयादनेनैव यथाक्रमम् ॥ 35 ॥
2.22.m: Or with "Payo 'si", he should duly strike Svargapatrī. / With this very hymn, he should bind it in due order.

2.22.s:
imāṃ khanāmītyanayā māṣaparṇīṃ tathā khanet ..
dvābhyāṃ cānarthasaktatvaprabadhnīyāditi śrutiḥ ..36..
2.22.d:
इमां खनामीत्यनया माषपर्णीं तथा खनेत् ॥
द्वाभ्यां चानर्थसक्तत्वप्रबध्नीयादिति श्रुतिः ॥36॥
2.22.m: With "Imāṃ khanāmi", he should likewise dig up Māṣaparṇī. / And with two [verses], because it clings without purpose, he should tie it, so says the scripture.

2.22.s:
tataḥ khaṇḍārikāṃ khanyādrājā tvāṃ varuṇaḥ khanet..
ṛcānayā samastena sūktenābandhanaṃ bhavet ..37..
2.22.d:
ततः खण्डारिकां खन्याद्राजा त्वां वरुणः खनेत्॥
ऋचानया समस्तेन सूक्तेनाबन्धनं भवेत् ॥37॥
2.22.m: Then he should dig up Khaṇḍārikā with the verse "Rājā tvāṃ varuṇaḥ khanat". / With the entire hymn, its binding should take place.

2.22.s:
ekārkaprabhṛtīnāṃ tu liṅgaḥ kalpyaṃ phalaṃ budhaiḥ ..
sāmīyātvāha varuṇetyevamādiṣu saṃśritāḥ .. 38 ..
2.22.d:
एकार्कप्रभृतीनां तु लिङ्गः कल्प्यं फलं बुधैः ॥
सामीयात्वाह वरुणेत्येवमादिषु संश्रिताः ॥ 38 ॥
2.22.m: For [amulets] beginning with Ekārka, however, the fruit is to be conceived by the wise from the characteristic marks, / based on [mantras] such as "Sāmīyā tvāha varuṇa" and others.

2.22.s:
sāmīdayaḥ padārthāste upaklṛptāstathā smṛtāḥ ..
dravyaistaistu maṇiṃ kuryādāmnāyoktairyathāvidhi .. 39 ..
2.22.d:
सामीदयः पदार्थास्ते उपक्लृप्तास्तथा स्मृताः ॥
द्रव्यैस्तैस्तु मणिं कुर्यादाम्नायोक्तैर्यथाविधि ॥ 39 ॥
2.22.m: The substances beginning with Sāmī are handed down as prepared in that manner. / With these substances, one should make an amulet according to the injunctions in the traditional texts,

2.22.s:
talliṅgena tu mantreṇa yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ ..
kuṣṭhasya maṇayaḥ pañca udapātre vidurbudhāḥ .. 2.109.40 ..
2.22.d:
तल्लिङ्गेन तु मन्त्रेण यथावदनुपूर्वशः ॥
कुष्ठस्य मणयः पञ्च उदपात्रे विदुर्बुधाः ॥ 2.109.40 ॥
2.22.m: duly in regular order, with the mantra indicating that characteristic. / The wise know five amulets of Kuṣṭha in a water vessel.

2.22.s:
pratyaikapāṭhasaṃskāra śuddhaye veti naḥ śrutam ..
caturasraṃ prabadhnīyānmaṇimañjanavattathā .. 41 ..
2.22.d:
प्रत्यैकपाठसंस्कार शुद्धये वेति नः श्रुतम् ॥
चतुरस्रं प्रबध्नीयान्मणिमञ्जनवत्तथा ॥ 41 ॥
2.22.m: Or, as we have heard, for purification through individual recitation and consecration, / he should bind a four-cornered amulet just like collyrium.

2.22.s:
saindhavaṃ lavaṇaṃ siddhamubhayatra parigrahāt ..
kuryādvākṣyaṃ ca saṃskāraṃ vyāghratyapamaṇau tathā..42 ..
2.22.d:
सैन्धवं लवणं सिद्धमुभयत्र परिग्रहात् ॥
कुर्याद्वाक्ष्यं च संस्कारं व्याघ्रत्यपमणौ तथा॥42 ॥
2.22.m: Rock salt is perfected from grasping it in both places. / He should also perform the tree consecration on the amulet against tigers.

2.22.s:
caturasrau tu kartavyau maṇī kāraṇakālajau ..
naimittikāśca maṇayo maṇayaḥ saṃviduśca ye .. 43 ..
2.22.d:
चतुरस्रौ तु कर्तव्यौ मणी कारणकालजौ ॥
नैमित्तिकाश्च मणयो मणयः संविदुश्च ये ॥ 43 ॥
2.22.m: Two four-cornered amulets should be made, produced by the occasion and the time. / And those amulets that are occasional, and those amulets that are known [as regular]—

2.22.s:
svaṃsvaṃ mantraṃ bhavetteṣāmiti me niścitā matiḥ ..
naimittikānāṃ ghorāste teṣāṃ naimittikaṃ bhavet .. 44 ..
2.22.d:
स्वंस्वं मन्त्रं भवेत्तेषामिति मे निश्चिता मतिः ॥
नैमित्तिकानां घोरास्ते तेषां नैमित्तिकं भवेत् ॥ 44 ॥
2.22.m: each has its own mantra; such is my settled opinion. / The terrible ones among the occasional amulets have an occasional [rite].

2.22.s:
sampadānāṃ tathā madhye sāmpadaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
sīmātryātvāhetyanena sīmasaṃ janavadbhavet .. 45 ..
2.22.d:
सम्पदानां तथा मध्ये साम्पदं नात्र संशयः ॥
सीमात्र्यात्वाहेत्यनेन सीमसं जनवद्भवेत् ॥ 45 ॥
2.22.m: Likewise among the [amulets] of prosperity, it belongs to prosperity, there is no doubt here. / With "Sīmātryā tvāha", the lead should become like the people.

2.22.s:
piśācaśātanaḥ puṃsāṃ yātudhānavināśanaḥ ..
mantraliṅgādayaṃ jñeyo mantraścāsya pravakṣyate .. 46 ..
2.22.d:
पिशाचशातनः पुंसां यातुधानविनाशनः ॥
मन्त्रलिङ्गादयं ज्ञेयो मन्त्रश्चास्य प्रवक्ष्यते ॥ 46 ॥
2.22.m: It dispels piśācas for men and destroys yātudhānas. / This is to be known from the mark of the mantra, and its mantra will be stated:

2.22.s:
śarakāṣṭhe tu saṃyojya sīsaṃ kṛtveti buddhimān ..
bhārṅgīṃ jyāṃ dhanuṣaḥ kṛtvā bādhakenātha tena tata .. 47 ..
2.22.d:
शरकाष्ठे तु संयोज्य सीसं कृत्वेति बुद्धिमान् ॥
भार्ङ्गीं ज्यां धनुषः कृत्वा बाधकेनाथ तेन तत ॥ 47 ॥
2.22.m: Fixing [an arrow-head] of lead onto an arrow-shaft of reed, the wise man, / having made a bowstring of bhārṅgī on the bow, then with that tormentor,

2.22.s:
bhūmau piśācamālikhya bhagavena tu tāḍayet ..
uttareṇa śareṇaiva piśāco nāśamāpnuyāt .. 48 ..
2.22.d:
भूमौ पिशाचमालिख्य भगवेन तु ताडयेत् ॥
उत्तरेण शरेणैव पिशाचो नाशमाप्नुयात् ॥ 48 ॥
2.22.m: having drawn a piśāca on the ground, he should strike it with the bow; / with the following arrow indeed the piśāca will meet destruction.

2.22.s:
śaṃkudhāramaṇermantra anusūryamiti smṛtiḥ ..
prajñātavarṇaśābdāśca rohitasya parigrahaḥ .. 49 ..
2.22.d:
शंकुधारमणेर्मन्त्र अनुसूर्यमिति स्मृतिः ॥
प्रज्ञातवर्णशाब्दाश्च रोहितस्य परिग्रहः ॥ 49 ॥
2.22.m: The traditional rule for the mantra of the Śaṅkudhāra amulet is "Anusūryam". / The taking up of a red [hide] has a well-known color and sound.

2.22.s:
carmaṇaḥ syāttathā vargo rohitāsābhavecca gāḥ ..
śaṃkurnidhīyate yatra vistarārthaṃ tu carmaṇaḥ .. 2.109.50 ..
2.22.d:
चर्मणः स्यात्तथा वर्गो रोहितासाभवेच्च गाः ॥
शंकुर्निधीयते यत्र विस्तरार्थं तु चर्मणः ॥ 2.109.50 ॥
2.22.m: There should be a set of skins, and they should be cattle that are red. / Where a peg is fixed for the sake of stretching out the hide,

2.22.s:
tasmāddeśānmaṇiḥ kāryaḥ śaṃkurdhanaparigrahaḥ ..
maṇidhanaṃ ca dugdhaṃ syādupaviṣṭāya carmaṇi .. 51 ..
2.22.d:
तस्माद्देशान्मणिः कार्यः शंकुर्धनपरिग्रहः ॥
मणिधनं च दुग्धं स्यादुपविष्टाय चर्मणि ॥ 51 ॥
2.22.m: from that place the amulet is to be made, the peg being the receipt of wealth. / And the wealth of the amulet should be milk for him seated on the hide,

2.22.s:
yajamānāya dharmajña udapātraṃ tathāmayā ..
atikāmala rogaghnamāyuṣyaśca tathā maṇiḥ .. 52 ..
2.22.d:
यजमानाय धर्मज्ञ उदपात्रं तथामया ॥
अतिकामल रोगघ्नमायुष्यश्च तथा मणिः ॥ 52 ॥
2.22.m: for the sacrificer, O knower of dharma, likewise a water vessel with disease-curing [herbs]. / The amulet destroys severe jaundice and grants longevity.

2.22.s:
imaṃ me kuṣṭhetyanena pañcānāṃ syātparigrahaḥ ..
atyarthameva naiteṣāṃ jalaṃ kuṣṭhena saṃyutam .. 53 ..
2.22.d:
इमं मे कुष्ठेत्यनेन पञ्चानां स्यात्परिग्रहः ॥
अत्यर्थमेव नैतेषां जलं कुष्ठेन संयुतम् ॥ 53 ॥
2.22.m: With "Imaṃ me kuṣṭha", the acquisition of the five takes place. / Not excessively indeed is water combined with Kuṣṭha for these.

2.22.s:
satkṛtya pānayogatvādyajamānaḥ pibettataḥ .
maṇayaḥ pañcakuṣṭhe dvau maṇiśabdaparigraham .. 54 ..
2.22.d:
सत्कृत्य पानयोगत्वाद्यजमानः पिबेत्ततः ।
मणयः पञ्चकुष्ठे द्वौ मणिशब्दपरिग्रहम् ॥ 54 ॥
2.22.m: Having honored it, because it is fit for drinking, the sacrificer should then drink it. / There are five amulets; in Kuṣṭha two receive the designation of amulet.

2.22.s:
tulyena vidhinā kāryāḥ phalaṃ teṣāṃ pṛthakpṛthak ..
śirortināśanaḥ pūrvo dvitīyo viṣadūṣakaḥ .. 59 ..
2.22.d:
तुल्येन विधिना कार्याः फलं तेषां पृथक्पृथक् ॥
शिरोर्तिनाशनः पूर्वो द्वितीयो विषदूषकः ॥ 59 ॥
2.22.m: They should be made by equal procedure, [yet] their fruits are distinct: / The first destroys headache; the second destroys poison;

2.22.s:
tṛtīyaśca tathā prokto viṣamajvaranāśanaḥ ..
caturthaśca tathā proktaḥ satatajvaranāśanaḥ .. 56 ..
2.22.d:
तृतीयश्च तथा प्रोक्तो विषमज्वरनाशनः ॥
चतुर्थश्च तथा प्रोक्तः सततज्वरनाशनः ॥ 56 ॥
2.22.m: the third is declared likewise to destroy intermittent fever; / the fourth is declared likewise to destroy continuous fever;

2.22.s:
cakṣuṣyaḥ pañcamaḥ prokto maṇirbhārgavanandana ..
kṛtvodapātraṃ kuṣṭhāmbho navanītavimiśritam .. 57 ..
2.22.d:
चक्षुष्यः पञ्चमः प्रोक्तो मणिर्भार्गवनन्दन ॥
कृत्वोदपात्रं कुष्ठाम्भो नवनीतविमिश्रितम् ॥ 57 ॥
2.22.m: the fifth amulet is declared beneficial to the eyes, O son of Bhṛgu. / Having made a water vessel containing kuṣṭha-water mixed with fresh butter,

2.22.s:
bhūyaḥ kuṣṭhaṃ kṣipettatra maṇiṃ tatrāvatārayet ..
maṇibandhaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā toyaṃ tatpāyayennaram .. 58 ..
2.22.d:
भूयः कुष्ठं क्षिपेत्तत्र मणिं तत्रावतारयेत् ॥
मणिबन्धं ततः कृत्वा तोयं तत्पाययेन्नरम् ॥ 58 ॥
2.22.m: he should again throw Kuṣṭha into it and immerse the amulet there. / Then, having tied the amulet, he should make the man drink that water,

2.22.s:
lipyecca sarujaṃ deśamudapātrajalena tu ..
yāḥ purastādityanena maṇiḥ syāllavaṇasya tu .. 59 ..
2.22.d:
लिप्येच्च सरुजं देशमुदपात्रजलेन तु ॥
याः पुरस्तादित्यनेन मणिः स्याल्लवणस्य तु ॥ 59 ॥
2.22.m: and he should smear the painful area with water from the water vessel. / With "Yāḥ purastāt", there is an amulet of salt.

2.22.s:
piturvastrapuṭe baddhvā lavaṇasya tu tanmaṇim ..
ābandhe kuṣṭhavatsyācca yātudhānavināśanaḥ .. 2.109.60 ..
2.22.d:
पितुर्वस्त्रपुटे बद्ध्वा लवणस्य तु तन्मणिम् ॥
आबन्धे कुष्ठवत्स्याच्च यातुधानविनाशनः ॥ 2.109.60 ॥
2.22.m: Having tied that amulet of salt in a fold of his father's garment, / its tying should be like Kuṣṭha, and it destroys yātudhānas.

2.22.s:
vyāghrarūpa ityanena khaṃtavyaṃ vāṭarūṣakam ..
vyāghrarūpa iti dvābhyāmṛgbhyāmābandhanaṃ bhavet .. 61 ..
2.22.d:
व्याघ्ररूप इत्यनेन खंतव्यं वाटरूषकम् ॥
व्याघ्ररूप इति द्वाभ्यामृग्भ्यामाबन्धनं भवेत् ॥ 61 ॥
2.22.m: With "Vyāghrarūpaḥ", Vāṭarūṣaka is to be dug up. / With the two verses "Vyāghrarūpaḥ", the tying should take place.

2.22.s:
piśācanāśakastvevaṃ sa maṇiḥ syādasaṃśayam ..
evamevottarābhyāṃ ca bhavepratyabhicārakaḥ .. .. 62 ..
2.22.d:
पिशाचनाशकस्त्वेवं स मणिः स्यादसंशयम् ॥
एवमेवोत्तराभ्यां च भवेप्रत्यभिचारकः ॥ ॥ 62 ॥
2.22.m: That amulet is truly a destroyer of piśācas, without doubt. / In this very way, with the following two [verses], it counteracts sorcery.

2.22.s:
viṣkandasyetyanenāha triparṇī viśvabheṣajī ..
skandasyopari yaḥ skando bhavettasya vināśinī .. 63 ..
2.22.d:
विष्कन्दस्येत्यनेनाह त्रिपर्णी विश्वभेषजी ॥
स्कन्दस्योपरि यः स्कन्दो भवेत्तस्य विनाशिनी ॥ 63 ॥
2.22.m: With "Viṣkandasya", he said, Triparṇī is a universal remedy; / it destroys that skanda which occurs on top of a skanda.

2.22.s:
yasmādaṅgāditi bhavedgaṇāditvātparigrahaḥ ..
gaṇasya karma sāmānyaṃ pratisūktaṃ na kārayeta .. 64 ..
2.22.d:
यस्मादङ्गादिति भवेद्गणादित्वात्परिग्रहः ॥
गणस्य कर्म सामान्यं प्रतिसूक्तं न कारयेत ॥ 64 ॥
2.22.m: With "Yasmād aṅgāt", the grasping is due to its belonging to a class. / The rite of the class is common; he should not perform it hymn by hymn.

2.22.s:
gorācavāri karmāṇi hantavyānīvamādibhiḥ ..
pataṅgādyāśca catvāraḥ saṃskṛtya prāṇino budhaḥ .. 65 ..
2.22.d:
गोराचवारि कर्माणि हन्तव्यानीवमादिभिः ॥
पतङ्गाद्याश्च चत्वारः संस्कृत्य प्राणिनो बुधः ॥ 65 ॥
2.22.m: Actions of the bile-water of a cow are to be performed with these [mantras] and others. / The wise man, having consecrated the four living beings beginning with insects,

2.22.s:
tṛṣṇatvaptaiśca mantreṇa gātraṃ prakṣālayetkhilam ..
prathamena tu sūktena veṇupautre dravo maṇiḥ .. 66 ..
2.22.d:
तृष्णत्वप्तैश्च मन्त्रेण गात्रं प्रक्षालयेत्खिलम् ॥
प्रथमेन तु सूक्तेन वेणुपौत्रे द्रवो मणिः ॥ 66 ॥
2.22.m: should wash the entire body with the mantra "Tṛṣṇatvaptaiḥ". / With the first hymn, a liquid amulet in a bamboo vessel—

2.22.s:
veṇuḥ kuryādbhaveddharmo vākṣavaddevadāruṇaḥ ..
saṃskṛtya pūrvamantreṇa māṣakādīnpramardayet .. 67 ..
2.22.d:
वेणुः कुर्याद्भवेद्धर्मो वाक्षवद्देवदारुणः ॥
संस्कृत्य पूर्वमन्त्रेण माषकादीन्प्रमर्दयेत् ॥ 67 ॥
2.22.m: a bamboo [vessel] he should make; its dharma is like wood, made of Devadāru. / Having consecrated with the previous mantra, he should rub down the beans and other grains.

2.22.s:
gātrasaṃskārasahitaiḥ piṣṭairvā prakṛtirbhṛśam ..
kevalenaiva mantreṇa mardayettu vinaśyati .. 68 ..
2.22.d:
गात्रसंस्कारसहितैः पिष्टैर्वा प्रकृतिर्भृशम् ॥
केवलेनैव मन्त्रेण मर्दयेत्तु विनश्यति ॥ 68 ॥
2.22.m: Or, along with body-consecration, the nature [of the disease] is violently crushed with paste; / if he rubs down with the mantra alone, it perishes.

2.22.s:
tathā svalomaprabhṛtī vidhūlo dhūśiro yutiḥ ..
devapraveśaṃ jatunā sthagayitvā tu raktikā .. 69 ..
2.22.d:
तथा स्वलोमप्रभृती विधूलो धूशिरो युतिः ॥
देवप्रवेशं जतुना स्थगयित्वा तु रक्तिका ॥ 69 ॥
2.22.m: Likewise, beginning with his own hair, [...] / having sealed the entrance of deities with lac, the raktikā [seed]

2.22.s:
dūṣyā iti pratīkena kuryātpratisaraṃ maṇim..
kṛtvā dūṣaṇamāyuṣyaṃ tadā pratyabhivādakaḥ..2.109.70..
2.22.d:
दूष्या इति प्रतीकेन कुर्यात्प्रतिसरं मणिम्॥
कृत्वा दूषणमायुष्यं तदा प्रत्यभिवादकः॥2.109.70॥
2.22.m: with the initial words "Dūṣyāḥ", he should make the amulet into a protective thread. / Having counteracted [harm], granting long life, then it is a counter-salutation.

2.22.s:
ayaṃ pratisaraḥ pāṇau yātrākāle sapatnahā ..
sūtreṇānena badhnīyālliṅgātpratisaro paraḥ..71..
2.22.d:
अयं प्रतिसरः पाणौ यात्राकाले सपत्नहा ॥
सूत्रेणानेन बध्नीयाल्लिङ्गात्प्रतिसरो परः॥71॥
2.22.m: This protective thread on the hand slays enemies at the time of departure. / He should bind it with this cord; by its mark it is another protective thread.

2.22.s:
anena vidhinā vṛtraṃ nijaghāna śatakratuḥ ..
aśaṃsa iti mantreṇa prabadhnīyādyathāvidhi..72..
2.22.d:
अनेन विधिना वृत्रं निजघान शतक्रतुः ॥
अशंस इति मन्त्रेण प्रबध्नीयाद्यथाविधि॥72॥
2.22.m: By this procedure Śatakratu slew Vṛtra. / One should fasten [the amulet] according to rule with the mantra 'Aśaṃsa'.

2.22.s:
bhūtiśrīprabhṛtīnāṃ ca vighnamevaṃ karoti yaḥ ..
vināśanaṃ tasya bhavedābandhādyakṣanāśanam..73..
2.22.d:
भूतिश्रीप्रभृतीनां च विघ्नमेवं करोति यः ॥
विनाशनं तस्य भवेदाबन्धाद्यक्षनाशनम्॥73॥
2.22.m: And whoever causes an obstacle to prosperity, fortune, and the like, / his destruction occurs; from its binding, consumption is destroyed.

2.22.s:
jyāsūtraprothitāḥ sapta vaṃśaprāptāḥ samudbhavāḥ ..
rattayāntaravyavahitā garbhiṇyā uddhared budhaḥ .. 74..
2.22.d:
ज्यासूत्रप्रोथिताः सप्त वंशप्राप्ताः समुद्भवाः ॥
रत्तयान्तरव्यवहिता गर्भिण्या उद्धरेद् बुधः ॥ 74॥
2.22.m: Strung on a bowstring, seven [amulet-gems] obtained from bamboo and sprung from it, / separated by intervals of red seeds, the wise man should take for a pregnant woman.

2.22.s:
māse caturthe badhnīyānmantreṇānena buddhimān ..
ekaikasminnatīte tu māse sūtrāntare maṇiḥ .. 75..
2.22.d:
मासे चतुर्थे बध्नीयान्मन्त्रेणानेन बुद्धिमान् ॥
एकैकस्मिन्नतीते तु मासे सूत्रान्तरे मणिः ॥ 75॥
2.22.m: In the fourth month, the wise man should bind it with this mantra; / and as each month passes, a gem [is placed] in the interval of the cord.

2.22.s:
ekaikaṃ prakṣipeddhīmānsasūtraṃ paścimaṃ tathā ..
prācī digiti mantreṇa udīcī bhayanāśanī ..76 ..
2.22.d:
एकैकं प्रक्षिपेद्धीमान्ससूत्रं पश्चिमं तथा ॥
प्राची दिगिति मन्त्रेण उदीची भयनाशनी ॥76 ॥
2.22.m: The intelligent man should add one by one with its cord, and the last one likewise, / with the mantra 'The eastern quarter', and 'the northern' which destroys fear.

2.22.s:
akṣīyābhyāmityanena dāpyaḥ syādyakṣmanāśanaḥ ..
sandhānārthaṃ śītamagne rātrīmāteta mohanaḥ ..
mayūragosuravṛddhau dvau vetīti prakīrtitam ..77..
2.22.d:
अक्षीयाभ्यामित्यनेन दाप्यः स्याद्यक्ष्मनाशनः ॥
सन्धानार्थं शीतमग्ने रात्रीमातेत मोहनः ॥
मयूरगोसुरवृद्धौ द्वौ वेतीति प्रकीर्तितम् ॥77॥
2.22.m: With [the mantra] 'From both eyes', [an amulet] destroying consumption should be applied; / for healing, 'The cold of fire'; 'Night has spread out' is bewildering; / for the increase of peacocks and cattle, two [mantras beginning with] 'Ve' are proclaimed.

2.22.s:
proktāstathaite maṇayo nṛvīra kāmyā mayā sarvahitāya puṇyāḥ ..
yeṣāṃ hi bandho duritāpahārī bhayāpahaḥ kevalavṛddhikārī ..78..
2.22.d:
प्रोक्तास्तथैते मणयो नृवीर काम्या मया सर्वहिताय पुण्याः ॥
येषां हि बन्धो दुरितापहारी भयापहः केवलवृद्धिकारी ॥78॥
2.22.m: And thus these desired, meritorious amulet-gems have been spoken of by me, O hero among men, for the benefit of all, / whose binding indeed takes away misfortune, removes fear, and brings about unmitigated increase.

2.22.s:
iti śrīviṣṇudharmottare dvitīyakhaṇḍe mā0saṃ0 rāmaṃ prati puṣkaropākhyāne maṇibandhavarṇanannāma navottaraśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. .. 109..
2.110
rāma uvāca ..
bhagavañchrotumicchāmi karma kāmyamahaṃ nṛṇām ..
kṛtena yena kāmānāṃ naro bhavati bhājanam .. 1..
puṣkara uvāca ..
sarveṣāmeva kāmānāmīśvaro bhagavānhariḥ ..
tasya sampūjanādeva sarvānkāmānupāśnute .. 2 ..
snāpayitvā ghṛtakṣīraiścandanenānulepayet ..
śuklaiḥ sampūjya puṣpaiśca saptamasya baliṃ haret .. 3 ..
raktapittānnaro ghorānmucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
tailakṣaudraghṛtairdevaṃ snāpayitvā janārdanam .. 4 ..
bhasmatrayeṇānulipya sampūjya kusumaiḥ sitaiḥ ..
pañcamudgabaliṃ dadyādatīsārātpramucyate .. 5 ..
saṃsnāpya pañcagavyena dattvā pañcānulepanam ..
pañcasasyabaliṃ dattvā sukhaṃ kuṣṭhātpramucyate .. 6 ..
2.22.d:
इति श्रीविष्णुधर्मोत्तरे द्वितीयखण्डे मा0सं0 रामं प्रति पुष्करोपाख्याने मणिबन्धवर्णनन्नाम नवोत्तरशततमोऽध्यायः ॥ ॥ 109॥
2.110
राम उवाच ॥
भगवञ्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि कर्म काम्यमहं नृणाम् ॥
कृतेन येन कामानां नरो भवति भाजनम् ॥ 1॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
सर्वेषामेव कामानामीश्वरो भगवान्हरिः ॥
तस्य सम्पूजनादेव सर्वान्कामानुपाश्नुते ॥ 2 ॥
स्नापयित्वा घृतक्षीरैश्चन्दनेनानुलेपयेत् ॥
शुक्लैः सम्पूज्य पुष्पैश्च सप्तमस्य बलिं हरेत् ॥ 3 ॥
रक्तपित्तान्नरो घोरान्मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ॥
तैलक्षौद्रघृतैर्देवं स्नापयित्वा जनार्दनम् ॥ 4 ॥
भस्मत्रयेणानुलिप्य सम्पूज्य कुसुमैः सितैः ॥
पञ्चमुद्गबलिं दद्यादतीसारात्प्रमुच्यते ॥ 5 ॥
संस्नाप्य पञ्चगव्येन दत्त्वा पञ्चानुलेपनम् ॥
पञ्चसस्यबलिं दत्त्वा सुखं कुष्ठात्प्रमुच्यते ॥ 6 ॥
2.22.m:
Thus in the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara, in the Second Book, in the discourse of Mārkaṇḍeya, in the narrative of Puṣkara to Rāma, the hundred and ninth chapter, entitled 'Description of the Binding of Amulet-Gems'.
2.110 / Rāma said: / O Blessed One, I wish to hear the optional rites for human beings, / by performing which a man becomes a vessel for [the attainment of] his desires.
Puṣkara said: / The Blessed Lord Hari is the lord of all desires; / solely through worshipping Him, one obtains all desires.
Having bathed [Him] with ghee and milk, one should anoint [Him] with sandalwood. / Having worshipped [Him] with white flowers, one should offer an oblation of seven [grains].
A man is freed from terrible internal haemorrhage; there is no doubt about this. / Having bathed the god Janārdana with oil, honey, and ghee,
anointed [Him] with the three ashes, and worshipped [Him] with white flowers, / one should offer an oblation of five varieties of mung bean; he is completely freed from diarrhoea.
Having bathed [Him] with pañcagavya and applied the five ointments, / and having given an oblation of five grains, he is easily freed from leprosy.

2.22.d:
त्रिरसस्नापितं देवं त्रिसुगन्धेन लेपितम् ॥
कृत्वा दत्त्वा त्रिसूत्रं च बलिं कामाद्विमुच्यते ॥ 7 ॥
स्नापयित्वा तु तैलेन त्रिभिरुष्णैर्विलेपयेत् ॥
पञ्चमाषबलिं दत्त्वा वातव्याधिं विमुञ्चति ॥ 8 ॥
द्विस्नेहस्नपितं देवं शीतोष्णेनानुलेपितम् ॥
पञ्चभिः स्नापयित्वा च रसैर्देवं जनार्दनम् ॥ 9 ॥
अनुलिप्य च धर्मज्ञ तथा पञ्चसुगन्धिना ॥
पञ्चवर्णानि पुष्पाणि तथा दत्त्वा यथाविधि ॥ 2.110.10 ॥
धूपं च पञ्चनिर्यासं दत्त्वा चैवाप्यनुत्तरम् ॥
ततश्च पञ्चमधुरं बलिं सम्यङ् निवेदयेत् ॥ 11 ॥
अनेन रोगतः शीघ्रं मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ॥
विष्णुं सहस्रमूर्धानं चराचरगुरुं हरिम् ॥ 12 ॥
स्तुवन्नामसहस्रेण ज्वरान्सर्वान्व्यपोहति ॥
घृतेन स्नापितं देवं चन्दनेनानुलेपयेत् ॥ 13 ॥
2.22.m:
Having bathed the god with three juices, anointed Him with the three fragrances, / and given three cords and an oblation, one is freed [from disease] according to desire.
Having bathed [Him] with oil, one should anoint [Him] with the three pungent substances. / Having given an oblation of five black lentils, he leaves behind wind disease.
Having bathed the god with two fats and anointed [Him] with the cold and hot [substance], / and having bathed the god Janārdana with the five juices,
and anointed [Him], O knower of dharma, with the five fragrances, / having properly offered flowers of five colours,
and having offered an unsurpassed incense of five resins, / one should then properly present an oblation of the five sweet substances.
By this one is quickly freed from disease; there is no doubt about this. / Praising Viṣṇu, the thousand-headed Hari, the guru of the moving and unmoving,
with the thousand names, one dispels all fevers. / One should anoint the god, bathed with ghee, with sandalwood.

पञ्चभिर्जलजैः पुष्पैस्ततः सम्पूजयेद्विभुम् ॥
धूपं दद्यात्त्रिवारं च पञ्चगव्यं तथा बलिम् ॥ ॥ 14 ॥
पञ्चगौडं तथा राम बद्धो मुच्येत बन्धनात् ॥
त्रिशीतस्नापितं देवं त्रिशीतेनानुलेपयेत् ॥ 15 ॥
त्रिशीतैः कुसुमैः पूज्यं धूपं दद्यात्त्रिशीतलम् ॥
त्रिशीतं च बलिं दत्त्वा राजकोपाद्विमुच्यते 16 ॥
शीतोष्णस्नापितं देवं त्रिशीतैरनुलेपयेत् ॥
धूपं दत्त्वा च शीतोष्णं शीतोष्णं च तथा बलिम् ॥ 17 ॥
गुरुप्रसादमाप्नोति नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥
यमलस्नापितं देवं यमलेनानुलेपितम् ॥ 18 ॥
अभ्यर्च्य यमलैः पुष्पैर्धूपं च यमलं दहेत् ॥
यमलं च बलिं दत्त्वा सौभाग्यं प्राप्नुयान्नरः ॥ 19 ॥
सौभाग्यकामा नारी च सौभाग्यं महदाप्नुयात् ॥
सौभाग्यकामोऽपि नरः सौभाग्यं महदश्नुते ॥ 2.110.20 ॥
2.22.m:
Then one should worship the all-pervading Lord with five water-born flowers. / One should offer incense thrice, and likewise pañcagavya as an oblation,
and the five molasses preparations, O Rāma; one who is bound is freed from bondage. / One should anoint the god, bathed with the three cooling substances, with the three cooling substances.
He should be worshipped with three cooling flowers, and one should offer three cooling incenses. / And having given three cooling oblations, one is freed from the king's wrath.
One should anoint the god, bathed with cold and hot substances, with the three cooling substances. / Having offered an incense of cold and hot substances, and likewise an oblation of cold and hot substances,
one attains the favour of the guru; no doubt should be entertained here. / Having bathed the god with twin [substances] and anointed [Him] with twin [substances],
worshipped [Him] with twin flowers, one should burn twin incenses. / And having offered a twin oblation, a man attains good fortune.
A woman desiring good fortune attains great good fortune; / even a man desiring good fortune attains great good fortune.

2.22.d:
त्रिभिः संस्नापितं देवं सौभाग्यं महदाप्नुयात् ॥
त्रिभिः फलैः स्नापयित्वा त्रिसारेणानुलेपयेत् ॥21॥
त्रिशीतं च बलिं दद्याद्यशः प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमम् ॥
त्रितैलस्नापितं देवं त्रिरक्तेनानुलेपितम् ॥22॥
धूपयेन्महिषाक्षेण त्रिरक्तं च बलिं हरेत् ॥
रौद्रकर्म तु प्राप्नोति सिद्धिरस्ति न संशयः॥23॥
त्रिगन्धस्नापितं देवं त्रिशीतेनानुलेपितम् ॥
पूजयेच्छ्वेतपद्मानां सहस्रेण महाभुजम्॥ ॥ 24॥
निवेद्य परमान्नं च श्रियं प्राप्नोत्यनुत्तमाम् ॥
घृतेन स्नापितं देवं चन्दनेनानुलेपितम्॥25॥
परमान्नं बलिं दत्त्वा यथेष्टं काममाप्नुयात् ॥
घृतेन स्नापितं देवं चन्दनेनानुलेपितम् ॥26॥
अपूपैः परमान्नेन कुल्माषेण च पूजयेत् ॥
आम्रातकानां मुख्यानां ततस्त्वष्टाधिकं शतम् ॥ 27 ॥
2.22.m:
One [who worships] the god bathed with three [substances] attains great good fortune. / Having bathed [Him] with three fruits, one should anoint [Him] with the three essences.
And one should offer three cooling oblations; one attains unsurpassed fame. / The god bathed with three oils and anointed with three red substances,
one should perfume with guggulu incense and offer three red oblations. / One attains [success in] fierce acts; there is success, of this there is no doubt.
Having bathed the god with three perfumes and anointed [Him] with the three cooling substances, / one should worship the mighty-armed Lord with a thousand white lotuses.
And having offered sweet rice-pudding, one attains unsurpassed fortune. / The god bathed with ghee and anointed with sandalwood,
having given sweet rice-pudding as an oblation, one obtains one's desire as wished. / The god bathed with ghee and anointed with sandalwood,
one should worship with cakes, sweet rice-pudding, and half-cooked barley porridge. / Then, one hundred and eight chief hog-plum fruits,

2.22.m:
[and] given three metals as the dakṣiṇā, one attains the destruction of enemies. / The god bathed with three fruits and anointed with three red substances,
and having given three cooling oblations, and masculine-named flowers, / and various chief fruits bearing masculine names,
one attains the birth of a son; no doubt should be entertained here. / The god bathed with ghee and anointed with three red substances,
having made that very incense and given it, one should offer milk. / Having given an oblation of ghee-filled pastries, a man attains a livelihood.
The god bathed with milk and clarified butter and anointed with sandalwood, / that very incense should be given, and then jasmine flowers.
Offering an oblation of the five products of the cow, and likewise offering clarified butter into the fire, / and giving a cow, O fortunate one, a person obtains cattle.
Bathing the deity with a pair [of substances], anointing [him] with a pair, / worshipping [him] with pairs of flowers, one should burn paired incense.

त्रिलोहं दक्षिणां दत्त्वा गाणपत्यमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 41 ॥

2.22.m:
Offering a paired oblation, he should likewise offer unbroken grains / accompanied by sesame and white mustard, as well as ghee, milk, and clarified butter.
And giving a horse as the sacrificial fee, he obtains unsurpassed horses. / Having bathed the deity with clarified butter and likewise anointed [him] with clarified butter,
worshipping [him] with four [kinds of] flowers, offering incense of four equal parts, / and offering the three bearded grains and likewise the three beverages,
and sacrificing into the fire the three bearded grains combined with the three fats, / giving the three metals as the sacrificial fee, he attains the status of Gaṇapati.
Then, having bathed Janārdana with the three sweets, / he should anoint [him] with the three cooling [substances] and likewise worship [him] with camaka flowers.
He should burn incense with the three cooling [substances], and offer an oblation of the three sweets, / and likewise madhūka flowers, grapes, and dates.
He obtains friendship with all beings; there is no doubt about it. / Having bathed the deity with clarified butter, and likewise with orris root and turmeric,

he should anoint [him] with sandalwood and then worship [him] with jasmine flowers. / Having offered [food] accompanied by clarified butter and honey, and likewise guggulu incense,
and offering an oblation of the three bearded grains and likewise the three salts, a man, / giving gold as the sacrificial fee, obtains his desired knowledge.
Giving with devotion to the deity sandalwood, clarified butter, jasmine, / sweet rice milk, and guggulu, a person obtains all desires.

नरकाणां गणनमुदितं पापानां ते मया राम ॥
एतच्च भवति घोरं त्वनुबन्धकृतं मनुष्याणाम्॥20॥
2.112
राम उवाच ॥
जन्तुः कथं सम्भवति कथं चैव विपद्यते ॥
कथं देहान्तरं याति तन्ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः ॥ 1 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
विश्वस्यावरणं राम तथैवाण्डं न हेम यत् ॥
तथा प्राणिशरीरस्य पार्थिवत्वं महाभुज ॥ 2 ॥
आकाशे नरशार्दूल यथैवाण्डं व्यवस्थितम् ॥
सुषिरं तद्वदेवेह पुरुषस्य शरीरगम् ॥ 3 ॥
धारयन्ति यथा विश्वमण्डस्याभ्यन्तरे स्थिताः ॥
वाय्वग्निसोमाः सततं तथा देहं शरीरिणाम् ॥ 4 ॥
आधारभूते द्वे भूते आद्यन्ते सर्वदेहिनाम् ॥
प्रपद्यन्ते महाभाग कललत्वं हि तत्क्षणात् ॥ 5 ॥
करोति तत्र च ततः प्रवेशं कर्मचोदितः ॥
वायुभूतस्तथा जीवस्त्यक्त्वा भोगविवर्धनम् ॥
स्वर्गाद्वा नरकाद्देहं तिर्यग्योनावथापि वा ॥ 6 ॥
2.23.m:
The enumeration of hells for sins has been declared to you by me, O Rāma; / and this becomes terrible because of the binding consequences for human beings.
Rāma said: / How does a living being come into existence, and how does it perish? / How does it pass to another body? Explain that to me as I ask.
Puṣkara said: / The enclosure of the universe, O Rāma, is indeed the [cosmic] egg, which is not made of gold; / likewise, O mighty-armed one, is the earthly nature of a creature's body.
Just as the egg is stationed in space, O tiger among men, / exactly so here is the cavity located in the body of a man.
Just as wind, fire, and soma, stationed within the egg, / constantly sustain the universe, so do they sustain the body of embodied beings.
The two elements that serve as the foundation, at the beginning and the end of all embodied beings, / immediately attain the state of an embryo, O fortunate one.
And then, impelled by karma, the individual soul, having become wind, / makes an entrance there, having abandoned the body that promotes enjoyment, / whether from heaven, from hell, or from an animal womb.

राम उवाच ॥

भोगदेहश्च कः प्रोक्तस्तं ममाचक्ष्व पृच्छतः ॥ 1 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
आतिवाहिका गर्भस्य देहो भवति भार्गव ॥
केवलं तं मनुष्याणां मृत्युकाल उपस्थिते ॥ 2 ॥
याम्यैर्नरैर्मनुष्याणां तच्छरीरं भृगूत्तम ॥
6
नीयते याम्यमार्गेण नान्येषां प्राणिनां द्विज ॥ 3 ॥
मनुष्याः प्रतिपद्यन्ते स्वर्गं नरकमेव वा ॥
नैवाऽन्ये प्राणिनः केचित्सर्वं ते फलभोगिनः ॥ 4 ॥
शुभानामशुभानां वा कर्मणां भृगुनन्दन ॥
संचयः क्रियते लोके मनुष्यैरेव केवलम् ॥ 5 ॥
तस्मान्मनुष्यस्तु मृतो यमलोकं प्रपद्यते ॥
नान्यः प्राणी महाभाग फलयोनौ व्यवस्थितः॥6॥
2.23.m:
Thus that individual soul then enters the womb through the bondage caused by the power of karma; / then, having entered, deluded, it remains for six months, [though] eternal, as the Veda [declares].
2.113
Rāma said:
How does the soul, having abandoned the body of experience, enter the womb?
And what is meant by the body of experience? Explain that to me as I ask.
Puṣkara said:
The subtle transit body is the body of the embryo, O Bhārgava.
It belongs only to human beings when the time of death arrives.
That body of human beings is led by the messengers of Yama, O foremost of the Bhṛgus, / along Yama's path, and not that of other living beings, O twice-born.
Human beings attain heaven or hell;
no other living beings at all do so, for they all only experience the fruits [of past deeds].
The accumulation of auspicious or inauspicious deeds, O son of Bhṛgu,
is made in this world solely by human beings.
Therefore, a dead human goes to the realm of Yama;
no other living creature does, O fortunate one, as they remain in wombs destined for experiencing fruits.

pāśabaddhagalaḥ pāpaḥ pīḍyate vai yamāgrataḥ .. 11 ..
citraguptāstatastasya svargaṃ narakameva ca ..
nivedayanti dharmajña sa tu piṇḍāśanastataḥ .. 12 ..
tadā tyaktvā tu taddehaṃ pretadehaṃ prapadyate ..
pretaloke tu vasatirvarṣaṃ tasya tu kīrtitā .. 13 ..
2.23.d:
गच्छम्̐ल्लोके प्रपन्नस्य पुरुषस्य तथा यमः॥
योनीश्च नरकांश्चैव निरूपयति कर्मणाम्॥7॥
पूजनीयाश्च ते तेन वैवस्वतमपश्यत॥
मरणानन्तरं प्रोक्तं तिरश्चां गर्भसम्भवम् ॥8॥
वायुभूताश्च ते गर्भं प्रपद्यन्ते न संशयः ॥
मनुष्यस्तु मृतो राम नीयते यममन्दिरम्॥9॥
तथा कर्मानुरूपेण यमं पश्यत्यसौ ततः ॥
घोरं पापस्तथा धर्मे निविष्टः सौम्यदर्शनम् ॥ 2.113.10 ॥
धर्मिष्ठः पूज्यते तत्र ह्यासनेनोदकेन च ॥
पाशबद्धगलः पापः पीड्यते वै यमाग्रतः ॥ 11 ॥
चित्रगुप्तास्ततस्तस्य स्वर्गं नरकमेव च ॥
निवेदयन्ति धर्मज्ञ स तु पिण्डाशनस्ततः ॥ 12 ॥
तदा त्यक्त्वा तु तद्देहं प्रेतदेहं प्रपद्यते ॥
प्रेतलोके तु वसतिर्वर्षं तस्य तु कीर्तिता ॥ 13 ॥
2.23.m:
As he proceeds to that realm, Yama then determines
for the person the wombs and the hells according to his deeds.
And they [human beings] should revere him; without seeing Vaivasvata,
it is taught that after death, animals enter the womb.
And transformed into wind, they enter the womb without doubt;
but a dead human being, O Rāma, is taken to the abode of Yama.
Then, in accordance with his deeds, he beholds Yama:
as terrible if he is a sinner, and as gentle-looking if he is devoted to dharma.
The righteous person is honored there with a seat and water;
while the sinner, his neck bound with nooses, is tormented before Yama.
Then the Citraguptas announce heaven and hell for him,
O knower of dharma, and he then eats the funeral balls of rice.
Then, having cast off that [transit] body, he assumes a deceased body;
and his residence in the realm of the deceased is declared to last for one year.

2.23.s:
kṣuttṛṣṇe pratyahaṃ tatra bhavato bhṛgunandana ..
ahorātraṃ tu tatrāpi mānuṣyaṃ parikīrtitam .. 14 ..
āmaśrāddhāstathā dattā bhujyaṃte tatra mānavaiḥ ..
ativāhikadehāttu pretapiṇḍairvinā naraḥ .. 15..
na hi mokṣamavāpnoti piṇḍāṃstatraiva so'śnute ..
kṛte sapiṇḍīkaraṇe naraḥ saṃvatsarātparam .. 16 ..
pretadehaṃ samutsṛjya bhogadehaṃ prapadyate ..
tadādau bhujyate tatra yatstokaṃ bhṛgunandana .. 17 ..
bhogadehāvubhau proktau śubhāśubhakasaṃjñakau ..
bhogadehaṃ śubhaṃ tasya devarūpasya jāyate .. 18 ..
nānāprakāramaśubhaṃ nīrūpaṃ ghoradarśanam ..
yādṛśaṃ tasya mānuṣyaṃ rūpamāsītpurātanam .. 19 ..
kiñcittasya tu sādṛśyaṃ tatrāpi pratipadyate ..
bhuktvā sa bhogadehena yathākālaṃ triviṣṭapam .. 2.113.20 ..
2.23.d:
क्षुत्तृष्णे प्रत्यहं तत्र भवतो भृगुनन्दन ॥
अहोरात्रं तु तत्रापि मानुष्यं परिकीर्तितम् ॥ 14 ॥
आमश्राद्धास्तथा दत्ता भुज्यंते तत्र मानवैः ॥
अतिवाहिकदेहात्तु प्रेतपिण्डैर्विना नरः ॥ 15॥
न हि मोक्षमवाप्नोति पिण्डांस्तत्रैव सोऽश्नुते ॥
कृते सपिण्डीकरणे नरः संवत्सरात्परम् ॥ 16 ॥
प्रेतदेहं समुत्सृज्य भोगदेहं प्रपद्यते ॥
तदादौ भुज्यते तत्र यत्स्तोकं भृगुनन्दन ॥ 17 ॥
भोगदेहावुभौ प्रोक्तौ शुभाशुभकसंज्ञकौ ॥
भोगदेहं शुभं तस्य देवरूपस्य जायते ॥ 18 ॥
नानाप्रकारमशुभं नीरूपं घोरदर्शनम् ॥
यादृशं तस्य मानुष्यं रूपमासीत्पुरातनम् ॥ 19 ॥
किञ्चित्तस्य तु सादृश्यं तत्रापि प्रतिपद्यते ॥
भुक्त्वा स भोगदेहेन यथाकालं त्रिविष्टपम् ॥ 2.113.20 ॥
2.23.m:
There, hunger and thirst arise for him every day, O son of Bhṛgu;
and even there, a day and night is declared to be that of humans.
Uncooked śrāddha offerings given by men are consumed there;
without the funeral balls for the deceased, a man from the subtle transit body
does not obtain release; he eats the rice-balls right there.
When the sapiṇḍīkaraṇa rite is performed after one year, a man
casts off the deceased body and assumes the body of experience.
At that beginning, whatever little [deed] exists is experienced first, O son of Bhṛgu.
Two bodies of experience are taught, named auspicious and inauspicious;
an auspicious body of experience is born for him having the form of a deity.
The inauspicious one is of various kinds, formless and terrible to behold.
Whatever human form he previously had,
he obtains some resemblance to it even there.
Having enjoyed heaven with that body of experience according to the proper time,

2.23.s:
karmaṇyalpāvaśeṣe tu tridivādvinipātyate ..
tridivātpatitaṃ tasya bhogadehaṃ tu rākṣasāḥ .. 21 ..
2.23.d:
कर्मण्यल्पावशेषे तु त्रिदिवाद्विनिपात्यते ॥
त्रिदिवात्पतितं तस्य भोगदेहं तु राक्षसाः ॥ 21 ॥
2.23.m:
when only a small remnant of merit remains, he is cast down from heaven.
When his body of experience has fallen from heaven, rākṣasas

2.23.s:
bhakṣayanti tadā bhūmau vikṛtā bhīmadarśanāḥ ..
pāpe tiṣṭhati cetsvarge tena bhukta tathā dvija .. 22 ..
2.23.d:
भक्षयन्ति तदा भूमौ विकृता भीमदर्शनाः ॥
पापे तिष्ठति चेत्स्वर्गे तेन भुक्त तथा द्विज ॥ 22 ॥
2.23.m:
then devour it on the earth, deformed and terrible to behold.
If sin remains while heaven has thus been enjoyed by him, O twice-born,

2.23.s:
tadā dvitīyaṃ gṛhṇāti bhogadehaṃ tu pāpinam ..
bhuktvā pāpaṃ tu te paścāttena bhuktaṃ triviṣṭapam .. 23 ..
2.23.d:
तदा द्वितीयं गृह्णाति भोगदेहं तु पापिनम् ॥
भुक्त्वा पापं तु ते पश्चात्तेन भुक्तं त्रिविष्टपम् ॥ 23 ॥
2.23.m:
then he assumes a second, sinful body of experience.
Having experienced the sin, [or] if heaven was experienced by him afterwards,

2.23.s:
śucīnāṃ śrīmatāṃ gehe svargabhraṣṭo'bhijāyate ..
puṇye tiṣṭhati cetpāpaṃ tena bhuktaṃ tadā bhavet .. 24 ..
2.23.d:
शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे स्वर्गभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते ॥
पुण्ये तिष्ठति चेत्पापं तेन भुक्तं तदा भवेत् ॥ 24 ॥
2.23.m:
he who fell from heaven is born in the house of the pure and prosperous.
If merit remains while sin has thus been experienced by him,

2.23.s:
tasminsambhakṣite dehe śubhaṃ gṛhṇāti vigraham ..
karmaṇyalpāvaśeṣe tu narakādapi mucyate .. 25 ..
2.23.d:
तस्मिन्सम्भक्षिते देहे शुभं गृह्णाति विग्रहम् ॥
कर्मण्यल्पावशेषे तु नरकादपि मुच्यते ॥ 25 ॥
2.23.m:
when that [sinful] body has been devoured, he assumes an auspicious form.
When only a small remnant of his deed remains, he is released even from hell.

2.23.s:
yuktastu narakādyāti tiryagyonimasaṃśayam ..
tatrāpyaśeṣataḥ pāpaṃ na tadaśnāti bhārgava ..
tato'vaśeṣaṃ mānuṣyaṃ bhuṃkte'sau kṛtalakṣaṇaḥ ..26..
2.23.d:
युक्तस्तु नरकाद्याति तिर्यग्योनिमसंशयम् ॥
तत्राप्यशेषतः पापं न तदश्नाति भार्गव ॥
ततोऽवशेषं मानुष्यं भुंक्तेऽसौ कृतलक्षणः ॥26॥

2.23.s:
rajjuryathā syādbahutantubaddhā vikarṣaṇaṃ śaktimanī gurūṇām ..
svargāya puṇyaṃ narakāya pāpaṃ tathā nṛṇāṃ syādiha bhārgavāgrya .. 27 ..
2.114
puṣkara uvāca ..
jīvaḥ praviṣṭo garbhe tu kalalaṃ prati tiṣṭhati ..
mūḍhastu kalale tasminmāsamātraṃ hi tiṣṭhati ..1..
dvitīyaṃ tu tadā māsaṃ ghanībhūtaḥ sa tiṣṭhati ..
tasyāvayavanirmāṇaṃ tṛtīye māsi jāyate .. 2 ..
tvakcarmapañcame māsi ṣaṣṭhe romṇāṃ samudbhavaḥ ..
saptame ca tathā māsi prabodhaścāsya jāyate .. 3 ..
sa jīvo'pi hi māṇḍūkaḥ śīte śītāditobhyasuḥ ..
mūḍhastiṣṭhati dharmajña ṣaṇmāsāngarbhagastathā .. 4 ..
māturāhārapītaṃ tu saptame māsyupāśnute ..
aṣṭame navame māsi bhṛśamudvijate tadā .. 5 ..
jarāyuveṣṭito deho mūrdhni baddhāñjaliḥ sadā ..
madhye klībastu vāme strī dakṣiṇe puruṣastathā .. 6 ..
2.23.d:
रज्जुर्यथा स्याद्बहुतन्तुबद्धा विकर्षणं शक्तिमनी गुरूणाम् ॥
स्वर्गाय पुण्यं नरकाय पापं तथा नृणां स्यादिह भार्गवाग्र्य ॥ 27 ॥
2.114
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
जीवः प्रविष्टो गर्भे तु कललं प्रति तिष्ठति ॥
मूढस्तु कलले तस्मिन्मासमात्रं हि तिष्ठति ॥1॥
द्वितीयं तु तदा मासं घनीभूतः स तिष्ठति ॥
तस्यावयवनिर्माणं तृतीये मासि जायते ॥ 2 ॥
त्वक्चर्मपञ्चमे मासि षष्ठे रोम्णां समुद्भवः ॥
सप्तमे च तथा मासि प्रबोधश्चास्य जायते ॥ 3 ॥
स जीवोऽपि हि माण्डूकः शीते शीतादितोभ्यसुः ॥
मूढस्तिष्ठति धर्मज्ञ षण्मासान्गर्भगस्तथा ॥ 4 ॥
मातुराहारपीतं तु सप्तमे मास्युपाश्नुते ॥
अष्टमे नवमे मासि भृशमुद्विजते तदा ॥ 5 ॥
जरायुवेष्टितो देहो मूर्ध्नि बद्धाञ्जलिः सदा ॥
मध्ये क्लीबस्तु वामे स्त्री दक्षिणे पुरुषस्तथा ॥ 6 ॥

2.23.s:
tiṣṭhatyuttarabhāge tu pṛṣṭhasyābhimukhastathā ..
yasyāṃ tiṣṭhati sā yonau tāṃ tu vetti na saṃśayam .. 7 ..
sarvaṃ smarati vṛttāntaṃ tvārabhya janmatastathā ..
andhakāre ca mahati pīḍāṃ vindati bhārgava .. 8 ..
kīṭagandhena mahatā kalmaṣaṃ vindate param ..
mātrānīte jale pīte paraṃ śītamupāśnute .. 9 ..
uṣṇe bhukte tadā dāhaṃ paramāpnoti bhārgava ..
vyādhibhiḥ paramāṃ pīḍāṃ tīvrāṃ prāpnoti duḥsahām .. 2.114.10 ..
vyāyāme ca tathā mātuḥ klamaṃ mahadupāśnute ..
vyādhitāyāṃ tathā tīvrāṃ vedanāṃ samupāśnute .. 11 ..
bhavanti vyādhayaścāsya tatra ghorāḥ punaḥpunaḥ ..
na ca mātā pitā vetti tadā kaściccikitsakaḥ .. 12 ..
saukumāryādrujaṃ tīvrāṃ janayanti tu tasya tāḥ ..
ādhibhirvyādhibhiścaiva pīḍyamānasya dāruṇaiḥ .. 13 ..
2.23.d:
तिष्ठत्युत्तरभागे तु पृष्ठस्याभिमुखस्तथा ॥
यस्यां तिष्ठति सा योनौ तां तु वेत्ति न संशयम् ॥ 7 ॥
सर्वं स्मरति वृत्तान्तं त्वारभ्य जन्मतस्तथा ॥
अन्धकारे च महति पीडां विन्दति भार्गव ॥ 8 ॥
कीटगन्धेन महता कल्मषं विन्दते परम् ॥
मात्रानीते जले पीते परं शीतमुपाश्नुते ॥ 9 ॥
उष्णे भुक्ते तदा दाहं परमाप्नोति भार्गव ॥
व्याधिभिः परमां पीडां तीव्रां प्राप्नोति दुःसहाम् ॥ 2.114.10 ॥
व्यायामे च तथा मातुः क्लमं महदुपाश्नुते ॥
व्याधितायां तथा तीव्रां वेदनां समुपाश्नुते ॥ 11 ॥
भवन्ति व्याधयश्चास्य तत्र घोराः पुनःपुनः ॥
न च माता पिता वेत्ति तदा कश्चिच्चिकित्सकः ॥ 12 ॥
सौकुमार्याद्रुजं तीव्रां जनयन्ति तु तस्य ताः ॥
आधिभिर्व्याधिभिश्चैव पीड्यमानस्य दारुणैः ॥ 13 ॥
2.23.m:
It stands in the upper part facing the [mother's] back;
and in whatever womb it remains, it knows that without doubt.
It remembers all events from the moment of birth,
and in the deep darkness it experiences pain, O Bhārgava.
From the great smell of worms, it experiences intense misery;
when water brought in by the mother is drunk, it feels extreme cold.
When hot food is eaten, it then experiences intense burning, O Bhārgava;
and through illnesses it undergoes extreme, sharp, and unbearable suffering.
When the mother engages in exertion, it suffers great exhaustion;
and when she is sick, it likewise experiences sharp agony.
Frightful diseases afflict it there again and again,
and neither the mother, nor the father, nor any physician knows of it then.
Because of its tenderness, these diseases produce sharp pain for it,
as it is afflicted by dreadful mental and physical diseases.

2.23.s:
svalpamadhye'tha tatkālaṃ yāti varṣaśatopamam ..
santapyate tathā garbhe karmabhiśca purātanaiḥ .. 14 ..
manorathāni kurute sukṛtārthaṃ punaḥpunaḥ ..
janma cedahamāpsyāmi mānuṣye daivayogataḥ .. 15 ..
tataḥ karma kariṣyāmi yena mokṣo bhavenmama ..
nāsti mokṣaṃ vinā saukhyaṃ garbhavāse kathañcana .. 16 ..
garbhavāsaśca sumahalloke duḥkhaikakāraṇam ..
evaṃ vicintayānasya tasya varṣaśatopamam .. 17 ..
māsatrayaṃ tadbhavati garbhasthasya prapīḍyataḥ ..
tatastu kāle sampūrṇe prabalaiḥ sūtimārutaiḥ .. 18 ..
bhavatyavāṅmukho jantuḥ pīḍāmanubhavanparām ..
adhomukhaḥ saṃkaṭena yonidvāreṇa vāyunā .. 19 ..
niḥsāryate bāṇa iva yantracchidreṇa sajvaraḥ ..
yoniniṣkramaṇātpīḍāṃ carmotkartanasannibhām .. 2.114.20 ..
2.23.d:
स्वल्पमध्येऽथ तत्कालं याति वर्षशतोपमम् ॥
सन्तप्यते तथा गर्भे कर्मभिश्च पुरातनैः ॥ 14 ॥
मनोरथानि कुरुते सुकृतार्थं पुनःपुनः ॥
जन्म चेदहमाप्स्यामि मानुष्ये दैवयोगतः ॥ 15 ॥
ततः कर्म करिष्यामि येन मोक्षो भवेन्मम ॥
नास्ति मोक्षं विना सौख्यं गर्भवासे कथञ्चन ॥ 16 ॥
गर्भवासश्च सुमहल्लोके दुःखैककारणम् ॥
एवं विचिन्तयानस्य तस्य वर्षशतोपमम् ॥ 17 ॥
मासत्रयं तद्भवति गर्भस्थस्य प्रपीड्यतः ॥
ततस्तु काले सम्पूर्णे प्रबलैः सूतिमारुतैः ॥ 18 ॥
भवत्यवाङ्मुखो जन्तुः पीडामनुभवन्पराम् ॥
अधोमुखः संकटेन योनिद्वारेण वायुना ॥ 19 ॥
निःसार्यते बाण इव यन्त्रच्छिद्रेण सज्वरः ॥
योनिनिष्क्रमणात्पीडां चर्मोत्कर्तनसन्निभाम् ॥ 2.114.20 ॥
2.23.m:
Then, within that brief span, the time passes like a hundred years; / and thus he suffers in the womb because of his past deeds.
Again and again he forms wishes to perform good deeds: / 'If by the stroke of fate I attain human birth,
then I shall perform action through which my liberation may come about. / Without liberation there is no happiness whatsoever in dwelling within the womb.
And dwelling in the womb is the supreme, sole cause of suffering in the world.' / While he thus reflects, those three months
seem like a hundred years to him as he suffers within the womb. / Then, when the time is complete, by the powerful winds of birth,
the creature is turned upside down, experiencing extreme pain. / Facing downward, by the wind through the constricted vaginal passage,
he is driven out feverish, like an arrow through the opening of an engine. / From exiting the vaginal passage [he suffers] pain resembling the flaying of the skin,

janmajvarābhibhūtasya vijñānaṃ tasya naśyati .. 21 ..

karapatrasya saṃsparśānmāsamātraṃ vimohitaḥ .. 22 ..

and then, once born, he undoubtedly encounters intense cold. / Overcome by the fever of birth, his consciousness is destroyed.
From the touch of his mother's hands, he is then insensible; / from the touch like a saw, he remains bewildered for an entire month.
This origin of a creature in the womb has been told by me to you. / In sequence I speak to you; tell that truth, O knower of dharma.
2.115
Rāma said: / O lord, you ought to explain to me the entire body; / for this indeed is the highest knowledge, and you know it, O mighty-armed one.
Puṣkara said: / Earth is to be known as having five qualities, water is to be known as having four qualities, / fire, O Rāma, has three qualities, and wind is regarded as having two qualities.
Ether in that regard is always to be known by the wise as having one quality. / Sound, touch, form, taste, and smell as the fifth—
one should know [all five] as the qualities of earth; [those of water] lack smell at the end; / while those lacking taste and smell are proclaimed to belong to fire.

2.23.m:
O foremost of the Bhṛgus, smell, taste, and form do not belong to wind; / and smell, taste, form, and touch are not found in ether.
Taste, smell, form, touch, and sound: / these are proclaimed as the principal qualities of earth and the rest, O descendant of Bhṛgu.
The channels, the sense of hearing, and emptiness arise from ether. / Inhalation and exhalation, movement, speech, and touch:
the wise person should know all these as belonging to wind. / Form, vision, digestion, bile, heat,
intellect, complexion, strength, luster, radiance, and valour: / all these one should know as fiery in embodied beings.
Here, belonging to water are the sense of taste, sweat, moisture, fat, / chyle, blood, semen, urine and so forth, as well as the collection of fluids in the body,
coldness, unctuousness, O knower of dharma, and phlegm. / Know that the earthy elements here are the breath, hair, nails, and so forth,

2.23.m:
desire, anger, fear, joy, nature of virtue and vice, / shape, voice and complexion, consciousness and the rest, and lifespan.
Those belonging to tamas are: loss of knowledge, negligence, indolence, thirst, hunger, / delusion, envy, defectiveness, grief, fatigue, and fear.
Desire, anger, valour, eagerness for sacrifice, talkativeness, / egoism, and contempt for others belong to rajas, O mighty-armed one.
Desire for dharma, longing for liberation, supreme devotion to Keśava, / courtesy, and resolve should be pointed out as belonging to sattva.
Skillful, irritable, timid, talkative, fond of quarrel, / and moving through the sky in dreams—a person would have an excess of wind.
Prematurely grey, prone to wrath, highly intelligent, fond of battle, / and seeing luminous objects in dreams—a person would have an excess of bile.
Steady in mind, steadfast in vigour, endowed with a firmly formed body, / and seeing water and white objects in dreams—a person would have an excess of phlegm.

2.23.m:
Chyle provides nourishment in the body, and blood enlivens; / flesh gives covering, and fat provides lubrication.
Bone is declared to be support, and marrow fills [the bones]; / semen produces offspring and increases vitality.
Radiant energy always provides vitality, and in it the living soul is situated; / it is the highest essence, even beyond semen, not yellow, resembling the heart.
I shall tell you the six principal limbs; listen: / the two arms, the two thighs, the head, and the abdomen.
And learn from me the six layers of skin recounted in this body: / externally, indeed, O Rāma, is the lower skin that holds the blood;
another is that which causes charm; the fourth causes cutaneous eruptions; / the fifth is the seat of abscesses; the sixth is regarded as holding vitality.
Seven membranes are remembered in the body; I shall tell you their characteristics: / one supports the flesh, O Rāma, where the vessels are located;

तत्त्वान्येतानि जानीहि चतुर्विंशतिसंख्यया ॥
येषामैक्यं महाभाग पुरुषः पञ्चविंशकः ॥ 2.115.40 ॥
संयुक्तस्तैर्वियुक्तश्च तथा मत्स्योदके उभे ॥
मनः संशयकृन्नित्यं तथा बुद्धिर्विवेचनी ॥ 41 ॥
आत्मा जीवः स्मृतो राम यो भोक्ता सुखदुःखयोः ॥
अव्यक्तो मिश्रितानीह रजःसत्त्वतमांसि च ॥ 42 ॥
2.23.m:
Likewise, their objects are five; I shall declare them hereafter: / excretion, pleasure, grasping, and walking;
these are the ten organs, [and] the mind is indeed their leader; / here are five organs of action and five organs of perception,
and here are five sense-objects and five gross elements. / Four are declared higher than the organs, O delight of the Bhṛgus:
the mind, the intellect, the self, and the unmanifest, O mighty-armed one. / The organs depend on them, and they are higher than the organs.
Know these principles to be twenty-four in number; / their unity, O fortunate one, is the twenty-fifth principle, the Cosmic Person.
Joined with them and separated from them, like both a fish and water, / the mind is ever producing doubt, and likewise the intellect is discerning.
The self is remembered as the living being, O Rāma, which is the experiencer of pleasure and pain; / the unmanifest is here the intermingled rajas, sattva, and tamas.

2.23.d:
पुरुषस्त्वपरो ज्ञेयो यश्च सर्वगतो महान् ॥
चतुर्विशतिकात्संख्याद्यः स नित्यः पृथक् स्थितः ॥ 43 ॥
एकत्रितानि तत्त्वानि पुरुषस्य तथैकतः ॥
न चैव व्यतिरिक्तानि तत्त्वानि पुरुषात्परम् ॥ 44 ॥
प्रकृतिः पुरुषो राम निष्फलः पञ्चविंशकः ॥
विकृतिस्तस्य विज्ञेया शेषस्तत्त्वगणो बुधः ॥ 45 ॥
सर्वतः पाणिपादोऽसौ सर्वतोक्षिशिरोमुखः ॥
पुरुषः स परो ज्ञेयः सर्वशक्तिस्तु सर्वतः॥46॥
नादिर्न मध्यो नैवान्तो व्याप्तिसम्भवयोर्द्वयोः ॥
यस्य जानन्ति मुनयो यस्तं वेद स वेदवित् ॥ 47॥
स याति परमं स्थानं यो वेत्ति पुरुषं परम् ॥
एतदेव च विज्ञानं प्रस्तुतं शृणु भार्गव ॥ 48 ॥
सप्ताशयाः स्मृता देहे शृणु तानपि भार्गव ॥
आशयो रुधिरस्यैकः कफस्य च तथा परः ॥ 49॥
2.23.m:
The Cosmic Person is to be known as another, great and all-pervading; / he who stands eternally distinct from the group of twenty-four,
the principles of the Cosmic Person are unified on the one hand; / and the principles are not separate from the supreme Cosmic Person.
Prakṛti [and] the Cosmic Person, O Rāma, is the partless twenty-fifth; / its modification is to be known by the wise [as] the rest of the group of principles.
Hands and feet are his everywhere, eyes, heads, and faces are his everywhere; / that supreme Cosmic Person is to be known, having all powers everywhere;
of whose two—pervasion and origin—the sages know neither beginning, middle, nor end; / he who knows him knows the Veda.
He goes to the supreme state who knows the supreme Cosmic Person; / and hear this very discernment introduced [now], O descendant of Bhṛgu.
Seven receptacles are recorded in the body; hear them also, O descendant of Bhṛgu: / one is the receptacle of blood, and another is that of phlegm;

2.23.d:
आमपित्ताशयौ चान्यौ ज्ञेयः पक्वाशयोऽपरः ॥
वायुमात्राशयौ चान्यौ आशया सप्त कीर्तितः॥2.115.50॥
स्त्रीणां गर्भाशयो राम पित्तपक्वाशयान्तरे ॥
अष्टमः स भवेत्तासां यत्र गर्भः स तिष्ठति ॥ 51 ॥
ऋतौ विकोशा भवति योनिः कमलवत्सदा ॥
गर्भाशये ततः शुक्र धत्ते रक्तसमन्वितम् ॥ 52 ॥
अन्यत्र काले मुकुला योनिर्भवति योषिताम् ॥
न्यस्तं शुक्रमतो योनौ नैति गर्भाशयं मुने ॥ 53 ॥
ऋतावपि च योनिश्चेद्वातपित्तकफावृता ॥
भवेत्तस्या विशौचार्थं नैव तस्याः प्रजायते ॥ 54 ॥
वृक्का तु पुष्पसप्लीहं हृत्कोष्ठाङ्गयकृद् घनाः ॥
तण्डुलश्च महाभाग निबद्धान्याशये तु ते ॥ 55 ॥
रसस्य पच्यमानस्य साराद्भवति देहिनाम् ॥
प्लीहा यकृच्च धर्मज्ञ रक्तफेनाच्च पुक्कसः ॥ 56 ॥
2.23.m:
the other two are the receptacles of undigested food and bile, [and] another is to be known as the receptacle of digested food; / the other two are the receptacles of wind and urine; seven receptacles are proclaimed.
For women, O Rāma, the womb is between the receptacle of bile and digested food; / for them that is the eighth, wherein the fetus resides.
In season, the vagina is always open like a lotus; / then it bears the semen united with blood in the womb.
At other times, the vagina of women is closed like a bud; / therefore, O sage, semen deposited in the vagina does not reach the womb.
Even in season, if the vagina is covered with wind, bile, and phlegm, / because of her impurity no offspring is born of her.
The kidneys, the lungs, the spleen, the heart, the viscera, the liver, solid masses, / and the taṇḍula, O fortunate one—they are bound to the receptacle.
From the essence of the chyle being digested of embodied beings arise / the spleen and the liver, O knower of dharma, and the lung from the foam of blood.

2.23.d:
रक्तकिट्टाच्च भवति तथा दण्डकसंज्ञकः ॥
मेदो रक्तप्रसादाच्च वृक्कयोः सम्भवः स्मृतः ॥ 57 ॥
रक्तमांसप्रसादाच्च भवन्त्यन्त्राणि देहिनाम् ॥
सावित्रिव्योमसंख्यानि तानि स्त्रीणां विनिर्दिशेत् ॥ 58 ॥
त्रिव्योमानि तथा स्त्रीणां प्राहुर्वेदविदो जनाः ॥
रक्तवायुसमायोगात्कालो यस्योद्भवः स्मृतः ॥ 59 ॥
कफप्रसादाद्भवति हृदयं पद्मसन्निभम् ॥
अधोमुखं तत्सुषिरं यत्र जीवो व्यवस्थितः ॥ 2.115.60 ॥
चैतन्यानुगता भावा सर्वे तत्र व्यवस्थिताः ॥
तस्य वामे तथा प्लीहा दक्षिणे च तथा यकृत् ॥ 61 ॥
दक्षिणे च तथा क्लोम पद्मस्यैव प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
स्रोतांसि यानि देहेऽस्मिन्कफरक्तवहानि तु ॥62॥
तेषां भूतानुगानां तु भवतीन्द्रियसम्भवः ॥
नेत्रयोर्मण्डलं शुक्लं कफाद्भवति पैत्तिकम् ॥ 63 ॥

2.23.d:
कृष्णं च मण्डलं वातात्तथा भवति मातृकम्॥
सर्वहृन्मण्डलं ज्ञेयं मातापितृसमुद्भवम् ॥ 64 ॥
पक्ष्ममण्डलमेकं तु द्वितीयं वर्त्ममण्डलम् ॥
शुक्ले तृतीयं कथितं चतुर्थं कृष्णमण्डलम्॥65॥
दृङ्मण्डलं पञ्चमं तु नेत्रं स्यात्पञ्चमण्डलम् ॥
अन्ये तु नेत्रभागे द्वे तथाऽपाङ्गकनीनिके॥66॥
याभ्यां नेत्रस्य जनिता मत्स्यसंस्थानता द्विज ॥
नासासमीपे कथितं तदपाङ्गेतिसंज्ञितम् ॥ 67 ॥
कपोलयोः समीपे तु तथा प्रोक्ता कनीनिका ॥
मांसासृक्कफजा जिह्वा मेदोऽसृक्कफमांसजा ॥ 68 ॥
वृषणौ च तथा ज्ञेयौ सर्वेषामेव देहिनाम् ॥
प्राणस्यायतानान्यत्र दशैतानि निबोध मे ॥69॥
मूर्धा च हृदयं नाभि कण्ठो जिह्वा निबन्धनम् ॥
रक्तं शुक्रं गुदो वस्तिस्तथा गुल्फौ च भार्गव ॥2.115.70॥
2.23.m:
and the black circle comes from wind, and likewise is maternal; / the entire circle of the pupil is to be known as originating from mother and father.
The circle of eyelashes is one, and the second is the circle of the eyelids; / the third is said to be in the white, and the fourth is the black circle;
the circle of vision is the fifth; the eye has five circles. / But there are two other parts of the eye: the outer and inner corners,
by which the fish-like shape of the eye is produced, O twice-born one. / That which is stated near the nose is designated the outer corner;
and near the cheeks the inner corner is spoken of. / The tongue is born of flesh, blood, and phlegm; born of fat, blood, phlegm, and flesh
the two testicles are to be known of all embodied beings. / Understand from me these ten seats of the breath here:
the head, the heart, the navel, the throat, the root of the tongue, / the blood, the semen, the anus, the bladder, and the ankles, O descendant of Bhṛgu.

2.23.d:
कण्डराः षोडश प्रोक्तास्तथा देहे शरीरिणाम् ॥
द्वे करस्थे तथा द्वे च चरणस्थे पृथक्पृथक् ॥ 71 ॥
चतस्रः पृष्ठगा ज्ञेया ग्रीवायां तावदेव तु ॥
जलानि षोडशैवात्र विभागस्तेषु कथ्यते ॥ 72 ॥
मांसस्नायुशिरास्थिभ्यः चत्वारस्तु पृथक्पृथक् ॥
मणिबन्धानि गुल्फेषु निबद्धानि परस्परम् ॥ 73 ॥
शंकूनि च स्मृतानीह हस्तयोः पादयोस्तथा ॥
ग्रीवायां च तथा मेढ्रे कथितानि मनीषिभिः ॥ 74 ॥
देहेऽस्मिंश्च तथा ज्ञेयाश्चतस्रो मांसरज्जवः॥
पृष्ठवंशोभयगते द्वे द्वे तत्र प्रकीर्तिते ॥ 75 ॥
तावन्त्यश्च तथाप्येतास्तासां बन्धनकारकाः ॥
सीवन्यश्च तथा सप्त पञ्च मूर्धानमाश्रिताः ॥ 76॥
एका मेढ्रगता चैका तथा जिह्वागता परा॥
अस्थ्नामत्र शतानि स्युस्त्रीणि षष्ट्यधिकानि तु॥77॥

2.23.d:

चत्वारिंशत्तथास्थीनि जंघयोस्तावदेव तु ॥
