ग्रीवापञ्चदशास्थीनि जत्र्वेकं च तथा हनुः ॥
भ्रूमूलं द्वे ललाटाक्षिगण्डनासा तथास्थिका ॥ 81 ॥
सर्जुकास्थालकैः सार्धमर्बुदैश्च द्विसप्ततिः ॥
द्वौ शङ्खकौ कपालानि चत्वार्येव शिरस्तथा ॥ 82 ॥
उरः सप्तदशास्थीनि पुरुषस्यास्थिसंग्रहः ॥
तथा चैवात्र सन्धीनां द्वे शते तु शताधिके ॥ 83 ॥
अष्टषष्टिश्च शाखासु षष्टिश्चैकविवर्जिता ॥
अन्तराधौ त्वशीतिश्च कथिता भृगुनन्दन ॥ 84 ॥

2.23.s:
na ca snāyuśatānyatra dve tu triṃśādhike mate ..
antarādhau tu kathitā hyūrdhvagāścaiva saptatiḥ .. 85 ..
ṣaṭkṛtāni ca śākhāsu kathitāni manīṣibhiḥ ..
pañcapeśīśatānyatra catvāriṃśattathordhvagāḥ .. 86 ..
catvāriṃśacchatānyatra tathā śākhāsu paṇḍitaiḥ ..
antarādhau tathā ṣaṣṭiḥ peśyastu kathitā budhaiḥ..87..
strīṇāṃ caivādhikā jñeyā triṃśatiścaturuttarā ..
stanayordaśa vijñeyā yonau rāma tathā daśa .. 88 ..
garbhāśaye tathā jñeyāścatasro garbhacintakaiḥ ..
triṃśacchatasahasrāṇi tathānyāni daśaiva tu .. 89 ..
ṣaṭpañcāśatsahasrāṇi śirāṇāṃ kathitāni tu ..
tā vahanti rasaṃ dehe kedāramiva kulyakāḥ .. 2.115.90 ..
abhyaṃgādi tathā sarvaṃ svedalepādikaṃ ca yat ..
dvisaptatistathā koṭyo romṇāṃ viddhi mahābhuja .. 91 ..
2.23.d:
न च स्नायुशतान्यत्र द्वे तु त्रिंशाधिके मते ॥
अन्तराधौ तु कथिता ह्यूर्ध्वगाश्चैव सप्ततिः ॥ 85 ॥
षट्कृतानि च शाखासु कथितानि मनीषिभिः ॥
पञ्चपेशीशतान्यत्र चत्वारिंशत्तथोर्ध्वगाः ॥ 86 ॥
चत्वारिंशच्छतान्यत्र तथा शाखासु पण्डितैः ॥
अन्तराधौ तथा षष्टिः पेश्यस्तु कथिता बुधैः॥87॥
स्त्रीणां चैवाधिका ज्ञेया त्रिंशतिश्चतुरुत्तरा ॥
स्तनयोर्दश विज्ञेया योनौ राम तथा दश ॥ 88 ॥
गर्भाशये तथा ज्ञेयाश्चतस्रो गर्भचिन्तकैः ॥
त्रिंशच्छतसहस्राणि तथान्यानि दशैव तु ॥ 89 ॥
षट्पञ्चाशत्सहस्राणि शिराणां कथितानि तु ॥
ता वहन्ति रसं देहे केदारमिव कुल्यकाः ॥ 2.115.90 ॥
अभ्यंगादि तथा सर्वं स्वेदलेपादिकं च यत् ॥
द्विसप्ततिस्तथा कोट्यो रोम्णां विद्धि महाभुज ॥ 91 ॥

2.23.s:
majjāyā medasaścaiva vasāyāśca tathā dvija ..
mūtrasya caiva pittasya śleṣmaṇaḥ śakṛtastathā .. 92 ..
raktasya ca rasasyātha kramaśoñjalayaḥ smṛtāḥ ..
ardhārdhābhyadhikāḥ sarvāḥ pūrvārdhāñjalitaḥ smṛtāḥ ..93..
ardhāṃjaliśca śukrasya tathārdhā ca tathaujasaḥ ..
rajasastu tathā strīṇāṃ catasraḥ kathitā budhaiḥ ..94..
samadhātoridaṃ proktaṃ pramāṇaṃ dehacintakaiḥ ..
vilakṣaṇāni dehāni nityameva śarīriṇām ..
teṣāṃ bhedena bhidyante maladoṣānurūpataḥ .. 95 ..
etaccharīraṃ maladoṣapiṇḍaṃ dhātvāśrayaṃ karmavaśānubaddham ..
mokṣāya yasyeha bhavetsa dhanyo mokṣe ca hetuḥ paramo hi viṣṇuḥ ..96..
2.23.d:
मज्जाया मेदसश्चैव वसायाश्च तथा द्विज ॥
मूत्रस्य चैव पित्तस्य श्लेष्मणः शकृतस्तथा ॥ 92 ॥
रक्तस्य च रसस्याथ क्रमशोञ्जलयः स्मृताः ॥
अर्धार्धाभ्यधिकाः सर्वाः पूर्वार्धाञ्जलितः स्मृताः ॥93॥
अर्धांजलिश्च शुक्रस्य तथार्धा च तथौजसः ॥
रजसस्तु तथा स्त्रीणां चतस्रः कथिता बुधैः ॥94॥
समधातोरिदं प्रोक्तं प्रमाणं देहचिन्तकैः ॥
विलक्षणानि देहानि नित्यमेव शरीरिणाम् ॥
तेषां भेदेन भिद्यन्ते मलदोषानुरूपतः ॥ 95 ॥
एतच्छरीरं मलदोषपिण्डं धात्वाश्रयं कर्मवशानुबद्धम् ॥
मोक्षाय यस्येह भवेत्स धन्यो मोक्षे च हेतुः परमो हि विष्णुः ॥96॥

2.24.s:
2.116
puṣkara uvāca ..
āyuṣi karmaṇi kṣīṇe saṃprāpte maraṇe nṛṇām ..
ūṣmā prakupitaḥ kāye tīvravāyusamīritaḥ .. 1 ..
2.24.d:
2.116
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
आयुषि कर्मणि क्षीणे संप्राप्ते मरणे नृणाम् ॥
ऊष्मा प्रकुपितः काये तीव्रवायुसमीरितः ॥ 1 ॥
2.24.m:
Puṣkara said:
When life and karman are exhausted, and death arrives for men,
the bodily heat, provoked in the body and stirred by a violent wind,

2.24.s:
śarīramuparudhyātha kṛtsnāndoṣānruṇaddhi vai ..
bhinatti prāṇasthānāni punarmarmāṇi caiva hi .. 2 ..
2.24.d:
शरीरमुपरुध्याथ कृत्स्नान्दोषान्रुणद्धि वै ॥
भिनत्ति प्राणस्थानानि पुनर्मर्माणि चैव हि ॥ 2 ॥
2.24.m:
obstructs the body, and then checks all the humoral faults;
it splits open the seats of breath and then the vital points;

2.24.s:
śaityātprakupito vāyuśchidramanviṣyate tataḥ ..
dve netre ca tathā karṇau dvau tu nāsāpuṭau tathā ..3..
2.24.d:
शैत्यात्प्रकुपितो वायुश्छिद्रमन्विष्यते ततः ॥
द्वे नेत्रे च तथा कर्णौ द्वौ तु नासापुटौ तथा ॥3॥
2.24.m:
the wind, provoked by coldness, then searches for an aperture:
the two eyes, and likewise the two ears, and the two nostrils,

2.24.s:
ūrdhva tu sapta cchidrāṇi saptakaṃ vadanaṃ tathā ..
etaiḥ prāṇo viniryāti prāyaśaḥ śubhakarmaṇām .. 4 ..
2.24.d:
ऊर्ध्व तु सप्त च्छिद्राणि सप्तकं वदनं तथा ॥
एतैः प्राणो विनिर्याति प्रायशः शुभकर्मणाम् ॥ 4 ॥
2.24.m:
and the upper apertures are seven, with the mouth being the seventh;
through these the breath departs, mostly in those of virtuous deeds;

2.24.s:
adhaḥ pāyurupasthaṃ ca chidradvayamudāhṛtam ..
chidradvayena tenātha mriyante'śubhakāriṇaḥ .. 5 ..
2.24.d:
अधः पायुरुपस्थं च छिद्रद्वयमुदाहृतम् ॥
छिद्रद्वयेन तेनाथ म्रियन्तेऽशुभकारिणः ॥ 5 ॥
2.24.m:
below, the anus and the genitals are declared as the pair of apertures;
through that pair of apertures, those who do unwholesome deeds die;

2.24.s:
mūrdhānaṃ yogināṃ bhittvā jīvo vrajati bhārgava ..
athavā svecchayā rāma yena cecchanti yoginaḥ .. 6 ..
2.24.d:
मूर्धानं योगिनां भित्त्वा जीवो व्रजति भार्गव ॥
अथवा स्वेच्छया राम येन चेच्छन्ति योगिनः ॥ 6 ॥
2.24.m:
splitting open the crown of the head, the soul of yogins departs, O Bhārgava,
or according to their own wish, O Rāma, by whatever [aperture] yogins desire.

2.24.s:
antakāle tu saṃprāpte prāṇāpāneṣvavasthitaḥ ..
tamasā saṃvṛte jñāne saṃvṛteṣu ca marmasu .. 7 ..
2.24.d:
अन्तकाले तु संप्राप्ते प्राणापानेष्ववस्थितः ॥
तमसा संवृते ज्ञाने संवृतेषु च मर्मसु ॥ 7 ॥
2.24.m:
When the hour of death has arrived, [the soul] remains in the prāṇa and apāna breaths;
when consciousness is shrouded by darkness, and the vital points are sealed,

2.24.s:
sa jīvo nābhyadhiṣṭhānaścālyate mātariśvanā ..
sa jīvaścālyamānastu karmabhistaiḥ purātanaiḥ .. 8 ..
2.24.d:
स जीवो नाभ्यधिष्ठानश्चाल्यते मातरिश्वना ॥
स जीवश्चाल्यमानस्तु कर्मभिस्तैः पुरातनैः ॥ 8 ॥
2.24.m:
that soul, seated at the navel, is moved by the wind;
and that soul, being moved by those past deeds,

2.24.s:
aṣṭāṅgāṃ prāṇavṛttiṃ tāṃ śanaiścyāvayate dvija ..
śarīraṃ prajahātyasmānniśvāsastu bhavettataḥ .. 9 ..
2.24.d:
अष्टाङ्गां प्राणवृत्तिं तां शनैश्च्यावयते द्विज ॥
शरीरं प्रजहात्यस्मान्निश्वासस्तु भवेत्ततः ॥ 9 ॥
2.24.m:
slowly casts off that eightfold activity of breath, O twice-born;
it abandons this body, and then the [last] out-breath occurs.

2.24.s:
cyavantaṃ jāyamānaṃ vā praviśantaṃ ca yoniṣu ..
paśyantyevaṃvidhaṃ siddhā jīvaṃ divyena cakṣuṣā .. 10 ..
2.24.d:
च्यवन्तं जायमानं वा प्रविशन्तं च योनिषु ॥
पश्यन्त्येवंविधं सिद्धा जीवं दिव्येन चक्षुषा ॥ 10 ॥
2.24.m:
Falling away or being born, or entering into wombs,
such a soul the perfected ones behold with divine vision.

2.24.s:
sa tu dehaparityāgakāle prāpte tadānagha ..
tatkṣaṇādeva gṛhṇāti śarīramativāhikam .. 11 ..
2.24.d:
स तु देहपरित्यागकाले प्राप्ते तदानघ ॥
तत्क्षणादेव गृह्णाति शरीरमतिवाहिकम् ॥ 11 ॥
2.24.m:
When the time for abandoning the body has arrived, O sinless one,
at that very moment it assumes a subtle body;

2.24.s:
ūrdhvaṃ bhajanti bhūtāni trīṇyasmāttasya vigrahāt ..
ākāśavāyutejāṃsi dve cādho bhṛgunandana .. 12 ..
2.24.d:
ऊर्ध्वं भजन्ति भूतानि त्रीण्यस्मात्तस्य विग्रहात् ॥
आकाशवायुतेजांसि द्वे चाधो भृगुनन्दन ॥ 12 ॥
2.24.m:
three elements depart upward from this form of his:
space, wind, and fire; and two go downward, O descendant of Bhṛgu:

2.24.s:
salilaṃ ca mahābhāga tathaiva ca vasundharā ...
evaṃ pañcatvamāpannaḥ puruṣastvabhidhīyate .. 13 ..
2.24.d:
सलिलं च महाभाग तथैव च वसुन्धरा ॥।
एवं पञ्चत्वमापन्नः पुरुषस्त्वभिधीयते ॥ 13 ॥
2.24.m:
water, O highly fortunate one, and likewise earth;
thus a person having attained fivefold dissolution is spoken of.

2.24.s:
evaṃ pañcatvamāpanne taddehamativāhikam ..
bhayānakairmahāghorairnānāveṣadharaistathā .. 14 ..
2.24.d:
एवं पञ्चत्वमापन्ने तद्देहमतिवाहिकम् ॥
भयानकैर्महाघोरैर्नानावेषधरैस्तथा ॥ 14 ॥
2.24.m:
When fivefold dissolution has thus occurred, that subtle body of his,
by terrifying, most dreadful [beings] wearing diverse attire,

2.24.s:
uccaistasya tadā baddhaṃ kālapāśena satvaram ..
nīyate kālapuruṣairyāmyaṃ mārgaṃ sudustaram .. 15 ..
2.24.d:
उच्चैस्तस्य तदा बद्धं कालपाशेन सत्वरम् ॥
नीयते कालपुरुषैर्याम्यं मार्गं सुदुस्तरम् ॥ 15 ॥
2.24.m:
tightly bound then by the noose of time, is swiftly
led by the minions of Yama along the path of Yama, which is exceedingly difficult to traverse;

2.24.s:
taptāmbarīṣasaṃkāśaṃ tvayoguṇanibhaṃ mahat ..
saṃtaptasikataṃ ghoraṃ tāmraparṇanibhaṃ tathā .. 16 ..
2.24.d:
तप्ताम्बरीषसंकाशं त्वयोगुणनिभं महत् ॥
संतप्तसिकतं घोरं ताम्रपर्णनिभं तथा ॥ 16 ॥
2.24.m:
resembling a heated frying pan, vast like an iron ball,
horrible with heated sand, and resembling copper leaves;

2.24.s:
ṣaḍaśītisahasrāṇi yojanānāṃ mahītalam ..
yamasya tu purī rāma ghorā saṃyamanī smṛtā .. 17 ..
2.24.d:
षडशीतिसहस्राणि योजनानां महीतलम् ॥
यमस्य तु पुरी राम घोरा संयमनी स्मृता ॥ 17 ॥
2.24.m:
eighty-six thousand leagues along the earth's surface,
the dreadful city of Yama, Saṃyamanī, is remembered, O Rāma;

2.24.s:
nīyate tena mārgeṇa tādṛśena tu tāṃ purīm ..
ākṛṣyamāṇaṃ puruṣairyāmyairghorairmahītale .. 18 ..
2.24.d:
नीयते तेन मार्गेण तादृशेन तु तां पुरीम् ॥
आकृष्यमाणं पुरुषैर्याम्यैर्घोरैर्महीतले ॥ 18 ॥
2.24.m:
along such a path he is led to that city,
being dragged over the surface of the earth by the dreadful minions of Yama;

2.24.s:
pīḍāmanubhavam̐statra mriyate na ca mānada ..
atyarthaviṣamaḥ proktaḥ sa mārgo ghoradarśanaḥ....
viśvarūpadharo rāma bhuvi śītāvṛto mahān ..
himaprapātabahulaścātiśītaḥ sudustaraḥ ..20..
2.24.d:
पीडामनुभवम्̐स्तत्र म्रियते न च मानद ॥
अत्यर्थविषमः प्रोक्तः स मार्गो घोरदर्शनः॥॥
विश्वरूपधरो राम भुवि शीतावृतो महान् ॥
हिमप्रपातबहुलश्चातिशीतः सुदुस्तरः ॥20॥

2.24.s:
andhakāravṛte durge garbhavāsopamastathā..
agnisaṃsparśavadanaiḥ kākakākolajambukaiḥ .. 21 ..
2.24.d:
अन्धकारवृते दुर्गे गर्भवासोपमस्तथा॥
अग्निसंस्पर्शवदनैः काककाकोलजम्बुकैः ॥ 21 ॥
2.24.m:
shrouded in darkness, impassable, and like dwelling in a womb;
with crows, ravens, and jackals whose mouths feel like fire,

2.24.s:
makṣikādaṃśamaśakairāvṛtaḥ sarpavṛścikaiḥ ..
bhakṣyamāṇo'pi tairjanturbhakṣyate cāpi rākṣasaiḥ .. 22 ..
2.24.d:
मक्षिकादंशमशकैरावृतः सर्पवृश्चिकैः ॥
भक्ष्यमाणोऽपि तैर्जन्तुर्भक्ष्यते चापि राक्षसैः ॥ 22 ॥
2.24.m:
covered with flies, gnats, mosquitoes, snakes, and scorpions;
even while being eaten by them, the creature is also devoured by rākṣasas.

2.24.s:
utkṛtyotkṛtya sahasā na ca prāṇairviyujyate ..
mudgaraiścūrṇyate ghoraistudyate lohakaṇṭakaiḥ .. 23 ..
2.24.d:
उत्कृत्योत्कृत्य सहसा न च प्राणैर्वियुज्यते ॥
मुद्गरैश्चूर्ण्यते घोरैस्तुद्यते लोहकण्टकैः ॥ 23 ॥
2.24.m: Torn to pieces again and again suddenly, he is not separated from his vital breaths; / he is crushed by dreadful clubs and pierced by iron thorns.

2.24.s:
kṣudhayā tṛṣayā caiva ghorayā cāpi pīḍyate ..
dahyamāno'tighoreṇa saikatena ca nīyate .. 24 ..
2.24.d:
क्षुधया तृषया चैव घोरया चापि पीड्यते ॥
दह्यमानोऽतिघोरेण सैकतेन च नीयते ॥ 24 ॥
2.24.m: He is afflicted by hunger and dreadful thirst; / burning from intensely hot sand, he is carried away.

2.24.s:
evaṃ saṃyāpyamānastu prāpyate yamamandiram ..
daśabhiḥ sa muhūrtaistu panthānamatidustaram .. 25 ..
2.24.d:
एवं संयाप्यमानस्तु प्राप्यते यममन्दिरम् ॥
दशभिः स मुहूर्तैस्तु पन्थानमतिदुस्तरम् ॥ 25 ॥
2.24.m: Being thus driven along, he is brought to the abode of Yama / after ten muhūrtas along an extremely impassable road.

2.24.s:
prāpnoti bhīmanirghoṣaṃ durgandhibhayadarśanam ..
tatkālaṃ sumahadvetti puruṣo devamāyayā .. 26 ..
2.24.d:
प्राप्नोति भीमनिर्घोषं दुर्गन्धिभयदर्शनम् ॥
तत्कालं सुमहद्वेत्ति पुरुषो देवमायया ॥ 26 ॥
2.24.m: He reaches [a place of] terrifying roars, foul-smelling and fearful to behold; / through divine delusion, the man perceives that duration as immense.

2.24.s:
pāpānurūpaṃ tatkālaṃ tasya tatrābhijāyate ..
kasyacidviśataṃ kālaṃ kasyacicchatasambhavam .. 27 ..
2.24.d:
पापानुरूपं तत्कालं तस्य तत्राभिजायते ॥
कस्यचिद्विशतं कालं कस्यचिच्छतसम्भवम् ॥ 27 ॥
2.24.m: In accordance with his sins, that period arises for him there: / for some, it is an entry of time, for others, [a state] arising for a hundred [years].

2.24.s:
kṣuttṛṣṇāsambhavāścaiva bhavantyatha mahābhayāḥ ..
daṇḍapiṇḍasya dharmajña pretatvamupajāyate .. 28 ..
2.24.d:
क्षुत्तृष्णासम्भवाश्चैव भवन्त्यथ महाभयाः ॥
दण्डपिण्डस्य धर्मज्ञ प्रेतत्वमुपजायते ॥ 28 ॥
2.24.m: Great terrors born of hunger and thirst arise; / O knower of dharma, the state of a deceased spirit befalls the bodily frame.

2.24.s:
preta loke sa vasati tataḥ saṃvatsaraṃ naraḥ ..
sodakumbhamatonnādyaṃ bāndhavaistasya dīyate .. 29 ..
2.24.d:
प्रेत लोके स वसति ततः संवत्सरं नरः ॥
सोदकुम्भमतोन्नाद्यं बान्धवैस्तस्य दीयते ॥ 29 ॥
2.24.m: The man dwells in the realm of the deceased for a year after that; / food along with a water-pot is given for him by his kinsmen.

2.24.s:
dinedine yaddharmajña tadbhuṅkte nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
na dīyate tu yasyaitatsa tu tatra yathā svayam .. 30 ..
2.24.d:
दिनेदिने यद्धर्मज्ञ तद्भुङ्क्ते नात्र संशयः ॥
न दीयते तु यस्यैतत्स तु तत्र यथा स्वयम् ॥ 30 ॥
2.24.m: O knower of dharma, he consumes daily whatever [is given], there is no doubt of this; / but for the one to whom this is not given, he [fares] there just as by himself:

2.24.s:
pūrvadattamathānnādyaṃ prāpnoti svayameva tu ..
svayameva na dattaṃ tu tathā dātā na vidyate .. 31 ..
2.24.d:
पूर्वदत्तमथान्नाद्यं प्राप्नोति स्वयमेव तु ॥
स्वयमेव न दत्तं तु तथा दाता न विद्यते ॥ 31 ॥
2.24.m: he obtains only the food and nourishment given by himself previously; / but if nothing was given by himself, then no giver is found.

2.24.s:
na cāstyudakadātā ca sa tu tatparitapyate ..
bāndhavaistūdakaṃ datta tatra tatrāsya jāyate.. 32 ..
2.24.d:
न चास्त्युदकदाता च स तु तत्परितप्यते ॥
बान्धवैस्तूदकं दत्त तत्र तत्रास्य जायते॥ 32 ॥
2.24.m: And there is no giver of water, so he suffers intensely there; / but the water given by kinsmen arises for him there at every step

2.24.s:
nadī śītajalā nāma bahupānīyasaṃyutā ..
māsimāsi ca yacchrāddhaṃ tasya tatra pradīyate .. 33 ..
2.24.d:
नदी शीतजला नाम बहुपानीयसंयुता ॥
मासिमासि च यच्छ्राद्धं तस्य तत्र प्रदीयते ॥ 33 ॥
2.24.m: as a river named Cold Water, filled with abundant water; / and whatever ancestral rite is offered for him month after month,

2.24.s:
tena tṛptimavāpnoti paramāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
mānuṣyeṇa tu māsena pitṛloke dinaṃ smṛtam .. 34 ...
2.24.d:
तेन तृप्तिमवाप्नोति परमां नात्र संशयः ॥
मानुष्येण तु मासेन पितृलोके दिनं स्मृतम् ॥ 34 ॥।
2.24.m: by that he attains supreme satisfaction, there is no doubt of this. / A month among humans is regarded as a day in the realm of the ancestors;

2.24.s:
pretaloke tu divaso mānuṣyeṇa vidhīyate ..
tasmāddinedine deyaṃ pretāyānnaṃ tu vatsaram .. 35 ..
2.24.d:
प्रेतलोके तु दिवसो मानुष्येण विधीयते ॥
तस्माद्दिनेदिने देयं प्रेतायान्नं तु वत्सरम् ॥ 35 ॥
2.24.m: in the realm of the deceased, however, a day is ordained according to human [reckoning]. / Therefore, food must be given daily to the deceased for a year.

2.24.s:
evaṃ sa yāpyamānastu prāpnoti yamamandiram ..
tataḥ paśyatyasau devaṃ pāpātmā ghoradarśanam .. 36 ..
2.24.d:
एवं स याप्यमानस्तु प्राप्नोति यममन्दिरम् ॥
ततः पश्यत्यसौ देवं पापात्मा घोरदर्शनम् ॥ 36 ॥
2.24.m: Being thus driven along, he reaches the abode of Yama; / then this sinful soul beholds the god of dreadful appearance.

2.24.s:
citraguptastatastasya jñātvā karma yathāvidham ..
ājñāpayati dharmajña śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham ..37..
2.24.d:
चित्रगुप्तस्ततस्तस्य ज्ञात्वा कर्म यथाविधम् ॥
आज्ञापयति धर्मज्ञ शुभं वा यदि वाशुभम् ॥37॥
2.24.m: Then Citragupta, having ascertained his deeds according to rule, / pronounces [the judgment], O knower of dharma, whether auspicious or inauspicious.

2.24.s:
tataḥ śmaśānikā nāma devā yāmyā bhayāvahāḥ ..
śītavātātapopetaṃ tadā rakṣanti mānavam .. 38 ..
2.24.d:
ततः श्मशानिका नाम देवा याम्या भयावहाः ॥
शीतवातातपोपेतं तदा रक्षन्ति मानवम् ॥ 38 ॥
2.24.m: Then the terrifying deities of Yama called Śmaśānikas / guard the man who is exposed to cold, wind, and heat,

2.24.s:
yatheha bandhane kaścidrakṣyate viṣamairnaraiḥ ..
preta piṇḍaistato dattairdehamāpnoti bhārgava .. 39 ..
2.24.d:
यथेह बन्धने कश्चिद्रक्ष्यते विषमैर्नरैः ॥
प्रेत पिण्डैस्ततो दत्तैर्देहमाप्नोति भार्गव ॥ 39 ॥
2.24.m: just as someone in prison is guarded here by harsh men. / Then, O descendant of Bhṛgu, he obtains a body from the funeral cakes given for the deceased,

2.24.s:
bhogadehamiti proktaṃ kramādeva na saṃśayaḥ ..
pretapiṇḍā na dīyante yasya tasya vimokṣaṇam .. 40 ..
2.24.d:
भोगदेहमिति प्रोक्तं क्रमादेव न संशयः ॥
प्रेतपिण्डा न दीयन्ते यस्य तस्य विमोक्षणम् ॥ 40 ॥
2.24.m: which is called the body of experience, [formed] gradually without doubt. / For the one for whom funeral cakes of the deceased are not offered, release

2.24.s:
śmaśānikebhyo devebhya ākalpaṃ naiva vidyate ..
tatrāsya yātanā ghorāḥ śītavātātapodbhavāḥ .. 41 ..
2.24.d:
श्मशानिकेभ्यो देवेभ्य आकल्पं नैव विद्यते ॥
तत्रास्य यातना घोराः शीतवातातपोद्भवाः ॥ 41 ॥
2.24.m: from the Śmaśānika deities does not occur even until an aeon; / there his dreadful torments arise from cold, wind, and heat.

2.24.s:
tataḥ sapiṇḍīkaraṇe bāndhavaiśca kṛte naraḥ ...
pūrṇe saṃvatsare dehamato'nyaṃ pratipadyate .. 42 ..
2.24.d:
ततः सपिण्डीकरणे बान्धवैश्च कृते नरः ॥।
पूर्णे संवत्सरे देहमतोऽन्यं प्रतिपद्यते ॥ 42 ॥
2.24.m: Then, when the sapiṇḍīkaraṇa is performed by kinsmen, / upon the completion of a full year, the man obtains another body beyond that.

2.24.s:
tataḥ sa narakaṃ yāti svargaṃ vā svena karmaṇā ..
tataḥ sa kālaṃ vasati karmaṇāmanurūpataḥ .. 43 ..
2.24.d:
ततः स नरकं याति स्वर्गं वा स्वेन कर्मणा ॥
ततः स कालं वसति कर्मणामनुरूपतः ॥ 43 ॥
2.24.m: Then he goes to hell or to heaven in accordance with his own karma; / then he dwells [there] for a period of time according to his deeds.

2.24.s:
arvāk sapiṇḍīkaraṇaṃ yasya saṃvatsarātkṛtam ..
pretatvamapi tasyāpi proktaṃ saṃvatsaraṃ dhuvam .. 44 ..
2.24.d:
अर्वाक् सपिण्डीकरणं यस्य संवत्सरात्कृतम् ॥
प्रेतत्वमपि तस्यापि प्रोक्तं संवत्सरं धुवम् ॥ 44 ॥
2.24.m: Even for him whose sapiṇḍīkaraṇa is performed prior to a year, / the state of the deceased is certainly declared to last for a full year.

2.24.s:
yairiṣṭaṃ vividhairyajñaiḥ pūjito yaiśca keśavaḥ ..
pretalokaṃ na te yānti tathā ye samare hatāḥ .. 45..
2.24.d:
यैरिष्टं विविधैर्यज्ञैः पूजितो यैश्च केशवः ॥
प्रेतलोकं न ते यान्ति तथा ये समरे हताः ॥ 45॥
2.24.m: Those by whom diverse sacrifices have been offered and by whom Keśava has been worshipped, / and those who have been slain in battle, do not go to the realm of the deceased.

2.24.s:
śmaśānikānāṃ devānāṃ bhavanti vaśagā na te..
pretalokaṃ prapadyante tathā ghoraṃ bhayāvaham .. 46 ...
2.24.d:
श्मशानिकानां देवानां भवन्ति वशगा न ते॥
प्रेतलोकं प्रपद्यन्ते तथा घोरं भयावहम् ॥ 46 ॥।
2.24.m: They do not fall under the power of the Śmaśānika deities, / [nor] do they enter that realm of the deceased which is dreadful and terrifying.

2.24.s:
evaṃ yāmyena mārgeṇa yānti pāpā narādhamāḥ ..
ārāmasadanaṃ yānti tathaiva drumaropakāḥ ..47..
2.24.d:
एवं याम्येन मार्गेण यान्ति पापा नराधमाः ॥
आरामसदनं यान्ति तथैव द्रुमरोपकाः ॥47॥
2.24.m: Thus sinful, vile men go by the road of Yama; / while those who plant trees go to an abode of grove-gardens.

2.24.s:
śītalena tu mārgeṇa phalapuṣpavatā sukham ..
chatradāśca sukhaṃ yānti mārgeṇa sasukhena te .. 48 ..
2.24.d:
शीतलेन तु मार्गेण फलपुष्पवता सुखम् ॥
छत्रदाश्च सुखं यान्ति मार्गेण ससुखेन ते ॥ 48 ॥
2.24.m: [They go] comfortably along a cool path rich with fruits and flowers; / and givers of umbrellas go happily by an easy road.

2.24.s:
yānamaśvatarīyuktamāsthāyopānahapradāḥ ..
vimānairyānadā yānti tathā śayyāsanapradāḥ .. 49 ..
2.24.d:
यानमश्वतरीयुक्तमास्थायोपानहप्रदाः ॥
विमानैर्यानदा यान्ति तथा शय्यासनप्रदाः ॥ 49 ॥
2.24.m: Givers of shoes go mounted on a conveyance harnessed to she-mules; / givers of vehicles go by aerial chariots, and so do givers of beds and seats.

2.24.s:
gṛhadāḥ savihārantu yānti tṛptā jalapradāḥ ..
bhakṣyairbhojyaistathā tṛptā yānti bhojanadāyinaḥ .. 50 ..
2.24.d:
गृहदाः सविहारन्तु यान्ति तृप्ता जलप्रदाः ॥
भक्ष्यैर्भोज्यैस्तथा तृप्ता यान्ति भोजनदायिनः ॥ 50 ॥
2.24.m: Givers of houses go along with pleasure halls, and givers of water go satisfied; / givers of meals go fully satisfied with edible foods and banquets.

2.24.s:
dīpapradāḥ prakāśena yānti mārgeṇa te sukham ..
pūjyamānā yamabhaṭairyānti bhaktā janārdanam .. 51 ..
2.24.d:
दीपप्रदाः प्रकाशेन यान्ति मार्गेण ते सुखम् ॥
पूज्यमाना यमभटैर्यान्ति भक्ता जनार्दनम् ॥ 51 ॥
2.24.m: Givers of lamps go comfortably along the path by means of light; / worshippers of Janārdana go while being venerated by the emissaries of Yama.

2.24.s:
nāsti teṣāṃ bhayaṃ kiñcidihaloke paratra ca ..
te tṛptāḥ sarvakāmaiśca tarasā yānti mānavāḥ .. .. 52 ..
2.24.d:
नास्ति तेषां भयं किञ्चिदिहलोके परत्र च ॥
ते तृप्ताः सर्वकामैश्च तरसा यान्ति मानवाः ॥ ॥ 52 ॥
2.24.m: There is no fear whatsoever for them in this world or in the next; / satisfied with all desires, those men travel swiftly.

2.24.s:
buddhiṃ samāsthāya tu sāttvikīṃ ye bhaktāḥ sureśasya janārdanasya ..
teṣāṃ gatistatra tu yatra rāma śvetāḥ pumāṃso gatasarvapāpāḥ .. 53 ..
2.117
rāma uvāca ..
bhagavañchrotumicchāmi ye narāḥ svargagāminaḥ ..
kena dharmabhṛtāṃ śreṣṭha tathā nirayagāminaḥ .. 1 ..
puṣkara uvāca ..
āśrameṣu yathokteṣu vartante ye dvijottamāḥ ..
svadharmasaktāḥ satataṃ te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ..2..
vartante ye mahīpāla rājadharmānusārataḥ ..
purohitamate yuktā rājānaḥ svargagāminaḥ .. 3 ..
prajāsukhe sukhaṃ yeṣāṃ tadduḥkhe ye ca duḥkhitāḥ ..
duṣṭanigrahakartāro jñeyāste svargagāminaḥ ..4..
svāmyarthe brāhmaṇārthe vā mitrakārye ca ye hatāḥ ..
gograhe nihatā ye ca te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ .. 5 ..
dehadhātūnparityajya salilāraṇyavahniṣu ..
anāśane vā dharmajña mṛtāḥ syuḥ svargagāminaḥ .. 6 ..
2.24.d:
बुद्धिं समास्थाय तु सात्त्विकीं ये भक्ताः सुरेशस्य जनार्दनस्य ॥
तेषां गतिस्तत्र तु यत्र राम श्वेताः पुमांसो गतसर्वपापाः ॥ 53 ॥
2.117
राम उवाच ॥
भगवञ्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि ये नराः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥
केन धर्मभृतां श्रेष्ठ तथा निरयगामिनः ॥ 1 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
आश्रमेषु यथोक्तेषु वर्तन्ते ये द्विजोत्तमाः ॥
स्वधर्मसक्ताः सततं ते नराः स्वर्गगामिनः॥2॥
वर्तन्ते ये महीपाल राजधर्मानुसारतः ॥
पुरोहितमते युक्ता राजानः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥ 3 ॥
प्रजासुखे सुखं येषां तद्दुःखे ये च दुःखिताः ॥
दुष्टनिग्रहकर्तारो ज्ञेयास्ते स्वर्गगामिनः ॥4॥
स्वाम्यर्थे ब्राह्मणार्थे वा मित्रकार्ये च ये हताः ॥
गोग्रहे निहता ये च ते नराः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥ 5 ॥
देहधातून्परित्यज्य सलिलारण्यवह्निषु ॥
अनाशने वा धर्मज्ञ मृताः स्युः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥ 6 ॥
2.24.m:
Those who, relying upon a pure mental disposition, are devoted to Janārdana, the lord of the gods— / their destination, O Rāma, is where radiant men reside, freed from all sins.
2.117 / Rāma said: / O venerable one, I wish to hear which men go to heaven, / and by what means, O best of upholders of dharma, [they go], as well as those who go to hell.
Puṣkara said: / The best of twice-born men who abide in the prescribed stages of life, / constantly dedicated to their own dharma, those men go to heaven.
Those who act in accordance with the royal duties, O protector of the earth, / kings intent upon the counsel of their royal priest, go to heaven.
Those whose happiness lies in the happiness of their subjects and who grieve in their sorrow, / who inflict restraint upon the wicked—they are to be known as goers to heaven.
Those who are slain for the sake of their master, for the sake of a brahmin, or on behalf of a friend, / and those who are killed in recovering cattle, those men go to heaven.
Those who have relinquished the bodily constituents in water, in the forest, or in fire, / or who die through fasting, O knower of dharma, go to heaven.

2.24.s:
tīrthayātrāprasaktāśca nityamadhvani karṣitāḥ ..
tapasā karṣitā ye ca te jñeyāḥ svargagāminaḥ .. 7 ..
madhumāṃsanivṛttāśca nivṛttā madhupānataḥ ..
kāmamaithunataścāpi vijñeyāḥ svargagāminaḥ .. 8 ..
mātāpitṛparā dāntā gurubhaktāḥ priyaṃvadāḥ ..
satyārjavaratā ye ca te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ .. 9 ..
vaivāhikānāṃ vastrāṇāṃ prapāṇāṃ ye pradāyinaḥ ..
udyānārāmakartāraste narāḥ svargagāminaḥ .. 10 ..
taḍāgakūpakartārastathā kanyāpradāyakāḥ ..
chatropānahadātāraste narāḥ svargagāminaḥ .. 11 ..
indhanānāṃ pradātārastathā gogrāmadāyinaḥ ..
gavāṃ śuśrūṣakā ye ca te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ .. 12 ..
paropakārasaktāśca parabandhavivarjakāḥ ..
pūjyapūjayitāraśca te narāḥ svargagāminaḥ .. 13 ..
svādhyāyasaktā dhīmanto guruśuśrūṣaṇe ratāḥ ..
upāsakāśca vṛddhānāṃ te jñeyāḥ svargagāminaḥ ..14..
2.24.d:
तीर्थयात्राप्रसक्ताश्च नित्यमध्वनि कर्षिताः ॥
तपसा कर्षिता ये च ते ज्ञेयाः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥ 7 ॥
मधुमांसनिवृत्ताश्च निवृत्ता मधुपानतः ॥
काममैथुनतश्चापि विज्ञेयाः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥ 8 ॥
मातापितृपरा दान्ता गुरुभक्ताः प्रियंवदाः ॥
सत्यार्जवरता ये च ते नराः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥ 9 ॥
वैवाहिकानां वस्त्राणां प्रपाणां ये प्रदायिनः ॥
उद्यानारामकर्तारस्ते नराः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥ 10 ॥
तडागकूपकर्तारस्तथा कन्याप्रदायकाः ॥
छत्रोपानहदातारस्ते नराः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥ 11 ॥
इन्धनानां प्रदातारस्तथा गोग्रामदायिनः ॥
गवां शुश्रूषका ये च ते नराः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥ 12 ॥
परोपकारसक्ताश्च परबन्धविवर्जकाः ॥
पूज्यपूजयितारश्च ते नराः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥ 13 ॥
स्वाध्यायसक्ता धीमन्तो गुरुशुश्रूषणे रताः ॥
उपासकाश्च वृद्धानां ते ज्ञेयाः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥14॥
2.24.m:
Those devoted to pilgrimage, perpetually worn out on the road, / and those emaciated by ascetic penance—they are to be known as goers to heaven.
Those who abstain from liquor and meat, who abstain from drinking alcohol, / and who abstain from lustful sexual intercourse are to be recognized as goers to heaven.
Those devoted to mother and father, self-controlled, devoted to their elders, speaking kindly, / and intent on truth and uprightness, those men go to heaven.
Those who provide wedding garments and public water-sheds, / and who create parks and pleasure-groves, those men go to heaven.
Those who construct reservoirs and wells, and those who give away maidens [in marriage], / and givers of umbrellas and shoes, those men go to heaven.
Those who provide firewood, and those who bestow cattle and villages, / and those who attend to cows, those men go to heaven.
Those devoted to helping others, free from binding others, / and who revere those worthy of reverence—such men go to heaven.
Wise men devoted to self-study, dedicated to serving their elders, / and who attend upon the aged—they should be known as goers to heaven.

2.24.d:
प्रतिश्रयप्रदातारस्तथा ये सत्रदायकाः ॥
भक्ता गोदेवविप्राणां ते नराः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥ 15 ॥
श्रोतारो ये च धर्माणां ये तथा यज्ञयाजिनः ॥
उपवासरता ये च ते ज्ञेयाः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥ 16 ॥
क्लेशाननुभवन्तीह शास्त्राध्ययनतत्पराः ॥
शास्त्राणां च हिते युक्तास्ते ज्ञेयाः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥17॥
आर्तप्राणप्रदा ये च ये च हिंसाविवर्जकाः ॥
अपीडकाश्च भूतानां ते नराः स्वर्गगामिनः॥ ॥18॥
दरिद्राय च दातारः प्रभवश्च क्षमान्विताः ॥
यौवनस्थाश्च ये शान्तास्ते नराः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥19॥
पौत्रदौहित्रसंयुक्ता ये तथा चिरजीविनः॥
प्रियङ्कराश्च बालानां ते नराः स्वर्गगामिनः॥
पोषकाणामनाथानां ये चैवोद्वाहकारिणः॥
द्विरागमनदा ये च ते नराः स्वर्गगामिनः॥21॥
ग्रहाणां पूजका ये च ये तथा श्राद्धकारिणः ॥
संविभागकरा ये च ते नराः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥ 22 ॥
2.24.m:
Those who provide shelter, and likewise those who provide free feeding-halls, / devoted to cows, gods, and brahmins—such men go to heaven.
Those who listen to the dharmas, and likewise those who perform sacrifices, / and those dedicated to fasting—they should be known as goers to heaven.
Those who endure hardships in this world intent upon the study of the śāstras, / and who are engaged in what is beneficial to the śāstras—they should be known as goers to heaven.
Those who grant life to the distressed, and those who refrain from injury, / and do not torment living beings—such men go to heaven.
Those who give to the poor, masters endowed with forbearance, / and those who, though in their youth, are peaceful—such men go to heaven.
Those endowed with grandsons and daughter's sons, who live long lives, / and who do what is pleasing to children—such men go to heaven; / and those who support orphans, who arrange marriages, / and who give for the bride's second arrival—such men go to heaven.
Those who worship the planets, and likewise those who perform ancestral rites, / and those who share their food—such men go to heaven.

2.24.d:
सर्वासां देवतानां च ये च पूजारताः सदा ॥
सर्वदानरता ये च ते नराः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥ 23 ॥
अहताश्च तथा तत्र कृत्वा कर्मातिदुष्करम् ॥
कालेनापि मृता राम ते नराः स्वर्गगामिनः ॥24॥
ये भक्तिमन्तो मधुसूदनस्य देवेश्वरस्याप्रतिमस्य नित्यम् ॥
सत्त्वेन हीना रजसा वियुक्तास्ते यान्ति नाकं सुरसंघपूज्याः॥25॥
2.118
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
महापातकिनो ये च ये च पातकिनो जनाः ॥
मांसाशिनो नरा ये च तथा येऽगम्यागामिनः ॥
परदाररता ये च ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥ 1 ॥
अतिक्रामन्ति ये भार्यां पीडयन्ति च ये नरान् ॥
ये सभास्ववन्यन्ते ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥ 2 ॥
बहुभार्याश्च भार्यासु वर्तन्ते न समं च ये ॥
ऋतुकालहरा ये च ते वै निरयगामिनः॥॥।
सम्यग्भर्तृषु या नार्यो वर्तन्ते नावलेपतः ॥
अप्रिये च तथा सक्ता ज्ञेयास्ता निरयङ्गमाः॥4॥
2.24.m:
Those who are always devoted to the worship of all deities, / and those devoted to all manner of gift-giving—such men go to heaven.
And having performed extremely difficult deeds there unslain, / dying only in the course of time, O Rāma, such men go to heaven.
Those who constantly possess devotion to Madhusūdana, the lord of gods, the matchless one, / free from sattva, separated from rajas—they go to heaven, worshipped by the host of gods.
Puṣkara said:
People who commit great sins, and those who commit lesser sins, / men who eat meat, and likewise those who approach forbidden women, / and those devoted to another's wife—they indeed go to hell.
Those who transgress against their wife and torment men, / and those who are despised in assemblies—they indeed go to hell.
Those who have many wives and do not behave equally toward their wives, / and those who neglect the fertile period—they indeed go to hell. / Women who do not behave properly toward their husbands out of arrogance, / and likewise are devoted to what is displeasing—they should be known as goers to hell.

2.24.s:

2.24.d:
भर्तारमवमन्यन्ते भाषन्ते विप्रियाणि च ॥
स्वातन्त्र्येण च वर्तन्ते ज्ञातव्या निरयङ्गमाः ॥ 5 ॥
राजशास्त्रोपदेशं ये संत्यज्य वसुधाधिपाः ॥
वर्तन्ते सर्वकार्येषु ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥ 6 ॥
वर्णाश्रमोक्तं वर्तन्ते धर्मं त्यक्त्वा तु ये नराः ॥
बहिःशास्त्रान्महाभाग ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥ 7 ॥
अयाज्ययाजिनो ये च कूटसाक्ष्यप्रदाश्च ये ॥
तथानृतरता ये च ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥ 8 ॥
व्यवहारेषु ये सक्ताः पक्षपाताभिधायिनः ॥
असम्यग्दर्शिनो ये च ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥ 9 ॥
प्रेक्ष्यमाणे परिजने मिष्टमश्नन्ति ये नराः ॥
असंविभज्य धर्मज्ञ ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥ 10 ॥
भृतकास्तु महाभाग कुर्वन्ते नैव ये भृतम् ॥
अनिर्दिष्टभुजश्चैव ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥11 ॥
वञ्चका भृतकानां च तथैवाश्रितवञ्चकाः ॥
वञ्चकाश्च तथाऽन्येषां ज्ञेया निरयगामिनः ॥ 12 ॥
2.24.m:
Those who despise their husband, speak unpleasant things, / and act according to their own independence—they should be known as goers to hell.
Those rulers of the earth who, abandoning the instruction of the royal treatises, / act in all matters [as they please]—they indeed go to hell.
Men who live abandoning the dharma prescribed for the social classes and stages of life, / outside the śāstras, O fortunate one—they indeed go to hell.
Those who sacrifice for those unfit to sacrifice, and those who give false testimony, / and likewise those devoted to falsehood—they indeed go to hell.
Those engaged in legal disputes who utter biased statements, / and those who do not see things impartially—they indeed go to hell.
Men who eat sweet delicacies while their dependents look on, / without sharing, O knower of dharma—they indeed go to hell.
Hired servants, O fortunate one, who do not do their hired work, / and those who eat what is not allotted to them—they indeed go to hell.
Deceivers of hired servants, and likewise deceivers of dependents, / and deceivers of others—they should be known as goers to hell.

2.24.s:

pāpaprotsāhakāścaiva te vai nirayagāminaḥ ..15..

yājyānāṃ ca gurūṇāṃ ca te vai nirayagāminaḥ .. 16 ..
tyāgino devatānāṃ ca vahnīnāṃ tyāginaśca ye ..
śāstrāṇāṃ tyāgino ye ca te vai nirayagāminaḥ .. 17 ..
bālakātithiviprāṇāṃ surāṇāṃ caiva mānada ..
ye ca pūrvabhujo nityaṃ te vai nirayagāminaḥ .. 18 ..
rajasvalāṃ ca ye yānti ye ca preṣyakarā striyam ..
viyoniṃ ye ca gacchanti te vai nirayagāminaḥ .. 19 ..
2.24.d:
कृतघ्ना निर्घृणा ये च परस्वादायिनश्च ये ॥
शठाचाराश्च मित्राणां ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥ 13 ॥
गवां पानप्रवृत्तानां ये तथा विघ्नकारिणः ॥
तथाऽन्येषां च भूतानां ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥ 14 ॥
धर्मकार्यप्रवृत्तस्य ये नरा विघ्नकारिणः ॥
पापप्रोत्साहकाश्चैव ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥15॥
त्यागिनस्त्वाश्रितानां ये ऋत्विजां त्यागिनश्च ये ॥
याज्यानां च गुरूणां च ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥ 16 ॥
त्यागिनो देवतानां च वह्नीनां त्यागिनश्च ये ॥
शास्त्राणां त्यागिनो ये च ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥ 17 ॥
बालकातिथिविप्राणां सुराणां चैव मानद ॥
ये च पूर्वभुजो नित्यं ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥ 18 ॥
रजस्वलां च ये यान्ति ये च प्रेष्यकरा स्त्रियम् ॥
वियोनिं ये च गच्छन्ति ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥ 19 ॥
2.24.m:
Those who are ungrateful, pitiless, and those who seize another's property, / and those who behave deceitfully toward friends—they indeed go to hell.
Those who cause an obstacle to cows engaged in drinking, / and likewise to other living beings—they indeed go to hell.
Those men who cause an obstacle to one engaged in an act of dharma, / and those who encourage sin—they indeed go to hell.
Those who abandon dependents, and those who abandon sacrificial priests, / their patrons, and their teachers—they indeed go to hell.
Those who abandon deities, and those who abandon the sacred fires, / and those who abandon the śāstras—they indeed go to hell.
Those who always eat before children, guests, brahmins, / and gods, O bestower of honor—they indeed go to hell.
Those who go to a menstruating woman, and those who go to a female servant, / and those who go to an unnatural orifice—they indeed go to hell.

2.24.d:
शुक्रं त्यजन्त्ययोनौ ये तथाकाशे च निर्घृणाः ॥
पर्वस्वपि च धर्मज्ञ ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥20॥
अनध्यायेषु ये राम स्वाध्यायमिह कुर्वते ॥
निन्दति च गुरून्ये वै ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥21॥
देवतानां च वेदानां ब्राह्मणानां च निन्दकाः ॥
पुराणचरितानां च ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥ 22 ॥
ये नास्तिका नरा राम ये च श्रद्धाविवर्जिताः ॥
अहङ्कारगृहीताश्च ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥23॥
कुकर्मसक्ता मनुजाः सुकर्मपरिवर्जकाः ॥
स्वामिमित्रद्रुहो ये च ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥24॥
ये च द्रोहरता राज्ञां ब्राह्मणानां गवामपि ॥
सुहृदामपि धर्मज्ञ ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥25 ॥
ये तु पैशुन्यसंसक्ताः परमर्मस्पृशोऽपि च ॥
अशुचश्च तथा मर्त्यास्ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥ 26 ॥
सोमविक्रयिणो ये च बीजविक्रयिणस्तथा ॥
आत्मविक्रयिणो ये च ज्ञेया निरयगामिनः ॥ 27 ॥
2.24.m:
Pitiless men who emit semen in an unnatural orifice, in open air, / or during the forbidden days of the lunar cycle, O knower of dharma—they indeed go to hell.
Those who engage in self-study on prohibited study days here, O Rāma, / and those who revile their teachers—they indeed go to hell.
Revilers of deities, of the Vedas, and of brahmins, / and of the stories of the Purāṇas—they indeed go to hell.
Those men who are materialists, O Rāma, and those devoid of faith, / and seized by egotism—they indeed go to hell.
Men attached to evil deeds, who abandon good deeds, / and who betray their masters and friends—they indeed go to hell.
Those who are intent on malice toward kings, brahmins, and cows, / and toward friends as well, O knower of dharma—they indeed go to hell.
Those mortals addicted to calumny, who touch upon another's vulnerable points, / and are impure—they indeed go to hell.
Those who sell soma, and likewise those who sell seed, / and those who sell themselves—they should be known as goers to hell.

2.24.d:
रजः पश्यन्ति धर्मज्ञ येषां वेश्मनि कन्यकाः ॥
शुल्के च दत्ता सा यैश्च ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥ 28 ॥
ब्रह्मेशकेशवानां च ये नरा भेदवादिनः ॥
तमोऽभिभूताः परितस्ते वै निरयगामिनः॥29॥
कुलजानां सपिण्डानां ये च पिण्डविलोपकाः ॥
अश्राद्धदाश्च पूर्वेषां ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥30॥
कामात्मानो नरा ये च ये तथार्थपरायणाः ॥
ये च धर्मद्विषो लोके ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥ 31 ॥
नाभिपश्यन्ति ये शक्त्या दीनमातुरमाश्रितम् ॥
आर्तं च नाभिधावन्ति ते वै निरयगामिनः ॥32॥
ये चावहासं कुर्वन्ति दीनानां मानगर्विताः ॥
अनागसं परिभवन्त्येते निरयगामिनः ॥ 33 ॥
पीडामथोत्पाद्य नरस्य राम यथाकथंचिन्नरकं प्रयाति ॥
तस्मात्प्रयत्नेन विवर्जनीया परस्य पीडा मनुजेन राम ॥॥। 34 ॥
2.24.m:
Those in whose house maiden daughters see their menses, O knower of dharma, / and those by whom she is given away for a bride-price—they indeed go to hell.
Those men who assert difference among Brahmā, Īśa, and Keśava, / utterly overcome by darkness—they indeed go to hell.
Those who omit the funeral cake for the sapiṇḍas born in their family, / and who do not offer the ancestral rites to their ancestors—they indeed go to hell.
And men whose nature is desire, and likewise those devoted [only] to wealth, / and those in the world who hate dharma—they indeed go to hell.
Those who do not look after the wretched, the sick, and their dependents according to their ability, / and do not run to help one who is distressed—they indeed go to hell.
And those proud with arrogance who mock the wretched, / and insult the innocent—these go to hell.
By causing torment to a person, O Rāma, one goes to hell in one way or another; / therefore, with effort, causing torment to another must be avoided by a person, O Rāma.

2.119
॥ राम उवाच ॥
नामानि नरकाणां च यातना विविधास्तथा ॥
भगवञ्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि पुंसां नरकगामिनाम् ॥ 1 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
तामिस्र मन्धतामिस्रं महारौरवरौरवौ ॥
नरकं कालसूत्रं च महानरकमेव च ॥2॥
संजीवनं महावीचिं तपनं संप्रतापनम् ॥
संघातं च सकाकोलं कश्मलं पूतिमृत्तिकम् ॥ 3 ॥
लोहशंकुं नृभीमं च मन्थानं शाल्मलिं नदीम् ॥
असिपत्रवनं चैव लोहकारं तथैव च ॥ 4 ॥
पातालेषु महाबाहो त्रींस्त्रीन्वृद्धिक्रमेण तु ॥
एकैकस्य तथैवाष्टौ दिक्षु चापि विदिक्ष्वपि ॥ 5॥
स्थितास्तथा ये विज्ञेया नरका घोरदर्शनाः ॥
यान्त्येते पापकर्माणो नरा येषु भृगूत्तम॥6॥
एकस्मिन्नरके केचित्क्रमादन्ये बहुष्वपि ॥
यांत्येते मानवा राम पीड्यमानाः पुनःपुनः॥7॥
2.24.m:
2.119
Rāma said:
O blessed one, I wish to hear the names of the hells, / and likewise the various torments of men who go to hell.
Puṣkara said:
Tāmisra, Andhatāmisra, Mahāraurava and Raurava, / the hell Kālasūtra, and Mahānaraka,
Saṃjīvana, Mahāvīci, Tapana, Saṃpratāpana, / Saṃghāta, Sakākola, Kaśmala, Pūtimṛttika,
Lohaśaṅku, Nṛbhīma, Manthāna, Śālmali, Nadī, / Asipatravana, and likewise Lohakāra.
In the netherworlds, O mighty-armed one, [arranged] in groups of three in order of increase, / and likewise eight for each one, in the cardinal and intermediate directions,
are situated the hells of dreadful appearance that should be known, / into which these men of evil deeds go, O foremost of the Bhṛgus.
Some men, O Rāma, go into one hell, others successively into many, / being tormented again and again.

2.24.d:
नरकाणां नराणां तु यातनाकारिणश्च ये॥
घोररूपास्तु ते प्रोक्ता दृष्टमात्रभयावहाः ॥ 8 ॥
मार्जारोलूकगोमायुगृध्रश्येनखराननाः ॥
गजाश्वोष्ट्रवराहाणां सिंहानां च तथा परे ॥ 9॥
गोधामहिषकाकानां मद्गुसारसयोस्तथा ॥
उरभ्राजपतङ्गानां सर्पमूषकयोस्तथा ॥ 10 ॥
अन्येषां चैव सत्त्वानां तथान्ये जठरा नराः ॥
स्कन्दाननास्तथैवान्ये कबन्धाकारदर्शनाः ॥ 11 ॥
भीमानना भयकरा नानायुधधरास्तथा ॥
उग्रवाचो दुराधर्षाः सर्पवृश्चिकवेष्टिताः ॥ 12 ॥
तैलद्रोण्यां नरान्क्षिप्त्वा ज्वालयित्वा हुताशनम् ॥
सुसमिद्धं नरान्कांश्चित्क्वाथयन्ति पुनःपुनः ॥ 13॥
अम्बरीषेषु चैवान्यांस्ताम्रपात्रेषु चापरान् ॥
अयःपात्रेषु चैवान्यान्द्रवद्वह्निकणेष्वपि ॥14॥
शूलेषु रोपितानन्याञ्शुष्काग्नावपरांस्तथा ॥
उत्कृत्य विपचन्त्येतानन्यांश्छित्वा तथा परान् ॥ 15 ॥

2.24.d:
कशाभिस्ताडयन्त्यन्यांस्तथान्यानपि मानवान् ॥
भोजयन्ति महाभाग वह्नितप्तानयोगुडान् ॥16॥
पांसूनपि तथैवान्यान्वान्तमन्यत्र चापरम् ॥
विष्ठामन्यत्र च कफं तथान्यत्र च कण्टकान् ॥ 17 ॥
अन्यत्र वह्निसंकाशास्तथा भार्गव वालुकाः ॥
पाययन्ति तथान्यत्र वह्निवर्णां च वारुणीम् ॥ 18 ॥
अन्यत्र नारकाणां ते छिन्दन्त्यङ्गानि भागशः ॥
पाटयन्ति तथान्यत्र करपत्रैः पुनःपुनः ॥ 19 ॥
पीडयन्ति तथान्यत्र कृत्वा यन्त्रेषु नारकान् ॥
उलूखलकृतानन्यान्मुसलैस्ताडयन्ति च ॥ 20 ॥
कुम्भीगतांस्तथान्यत्र कुम्भीतः किञ्चिदुद्गतान् ॥
घ्नन्ति मुद्गरकूटेन महतीं वेदनां गतान् ॥ 21 ॥
त्वचमुत्कृत्य चान्यत्र शुनां नरकवासिनः ॥
त्यजन्ति ते च भक्ष्यन्ते तीक्ष्णदन्तैर्मुहुर्मुहुः ॥ 22 ॥
2.24.m:
They strike others with whips, and other men as well, / O illustrious one, they force to eat iron balls heated in fire.
Likewise [they force] others [to eat] dust, and elsewhere others [to eat] vomit, / and elsewhere feces, and phlegm, and elsewhere thorns;
and elsewhere, O Bhārgava, sands resembling fire; / and elsewhere they force them to drink liquor colored like fire.
Elsewhere they cut the limbs of the denizens of hell limb by limb; / and elsewhere they tear them apart again and again with saws.
And elsewhere, placing the hell-dwellers in machines, they press them; / and placing others in a mortar, they strike them with pestles.
And elsewhere, those who are in pots or who have emerged slightly from a pot, / having attained great agony, they strike with iron mallets.
And elsewhere, having stripped off their skin, they cast the hell-dwellers to dogs, / and they are eaten by [dogs] with sharp teeth again and again.

2.24.d:
अन्धकारे तथान्यत्र भीमगन्धे भयावहे ॥
अत्युष्णे तैश्च पात्यन्ते गर्भवाससमे जनाः ॥ 23 ॥
काकैर्गोमायुभिः सर्पैर्वृश्चिकैर्मूषकैरपि ॥
मक्षिकाभिश्च भक्ष्यन्ते तेषामन्यत्र शासनात् ॥ 24 ॥
अन्यत्र शाल्मलिं घोरं संतप्तं तीक्ष्णकण्टकम् ॥
सर्पकीटादिबहुलमारोप्यन्ते नराधमाः ॥ 25 ॥
अन्यत्र च तथा घोरां सन्तप्तामयसः शिलाम् ॥
आलिङ्गन्ते सुदुःस्पर्शा तेषामेव तु शासनात् ॥26॥
अन्यत्रासेव्यवसतौ वसन्ति भयपीडिताः॥
तत्र तेषां तु नासाक्षिकर्णवक्त्रेषु मानद ॥ 27 ॥
प्रविशन्ति महाभोगाः कृमयो मांसभोजिनः ॥
क्षारनद्यां तथैवान्ये पात्यन्ते नारकान्मुहुः ॥28॥
बहुशीतान्धकारे च पात्यन्ते नरके परे ॥
रक्ततोयवहामन्ये प्रपद्यन्ते महानदीम् ॥29॥
असिपत्रवने चान्ये कृष्यन्ते भीमदर्शनाः ॥
तृष्णया क्षुधया चान्ये बाध्यन्ते तत्र मानवाः ॥ 30 ॥
2.24.m:
And elsewhere, into a dark, terribly foul-smelling, terrifying, / intensely hot place like the dwelling of a womb, people are thrown by them.
By crows, jackals, serpents, scorpions, and mice, / and by flies they are eaten elsewhere by their command.
Elsewhere the vilest of men are forced to climb a dreadful Śālmali tree, / scorching, with sharp thorns, filled with serpents, insects, and other vermin.
And elsewhere, by their very command, they embrace / a dreadful heated slab of iron, exceedingly painful to touch.
Elsewhere, afflicted with fear, they dwell in an unapproachable abode; / there, O giver of honor, into their nostrils, eyes, ears, and mouths
enter flesh-eating worms with large coils; / and likewise others are repeatedly cast into an alkaline river.
And others are cast into a hell of extreme cold and darkness; / others enter a great river carrying streams of blood.
And others of dreadful appearance are dragged through the forest of sword-leaves; / and other men are afflicted there with thirst and hunger.

2.24.d:
परान्नपानं लिप्सन्तस्ताड्यन्ते कूटमुद्गरैः ॥
पाययन्ति तथान्यत्र परान्यमभटास्तथा ॥ 31 ॥
तीव्रधूममधोवक्त्रान्बद्ध्वा वृक्षेषु मानद ॥
त्वचोत्कर्तनमन्यत्र तिलशः क्रियते भटैः ॥32॥
काष्ठान्यन्यत्र बध्यन्ते नारकाणां तथास्थिषु ॥
कूटागारप्रमाणैश्च तथा देहैर्भयार्दिताः ॥33 ॥
सूचीवक्त्रांस्तथान्यत्र याप्यन्ते क्षुधया भृशम् ॥
सिच्यन्ते च तथान्यत्र तैलेन च गुडेन च ॥34॥
सन्तप्तेन महाभाग भृशं दुःखप्रदायिनाम् ॥
अन्यत्र जातपिटकाः स्रस्तजिह्वाः सुविह्वलाः॥35॥
घोरातपविनिक्षिप्ता भक्ष्यन्ते च पिपीलकैः॥
सूत्रेणान्यत्र छिद्यन्ते पादतः प्रभृति क्रमात् ॥ 36 ॥
तिलशो भृगुशार्दूल नारकाः पर्वतोपमाः ॥
यावच्च तेषां मूर्धानं तावदेव पुनःपुनः ॥ 37 ॥
2.24.m:
Desiring the food and drink of others, they are beaten with iron clubs; / likewise elsewhere the soldiers of Yama force others to drink
sharp smoke, having tied them upside down to trees, O giver of honor; / elsewhere the flaying of skin is done bit by bit by the soldiers.
Elsewhere pieces of wood are bound to the bones of the hell-dwellers; / and distressed with fear, with bodies [puffed up to] the size of a peaked hall,
having needle-like mouths elsewhere, they are made to suffer greatly with hunger; / and elsewhere they are sprinkled with oil and with molasses,
heated, O illustrious one, which cause intense pain to them; / elsewhere, with boils formed, their tongues lolling out, exceedingly distraught,
cast down in terrible heat, they are eaten by ants; / elsewhere, beginning from the feet in order, with a thread are cut
into sesame-seed-sized bits, O tiger among the Bhṛgus, the mountain-like hell-dwellers, / all the way up to their heads, again and again.

2.24.d:
कृत्वा च पिष्टं पचनं पच्यन्तेऽन्ये तथा भृशम् ॥
अयःपात्रेषु चान्यत्र तीक्ष्णशङ्कुभिरायसैः ॥ 38 ॥
क्रियन्ते संयता घोरैः सन्तप्तेषु महाभुज ॥
आपोथ्यन्ते तथान्यत्र विनिगृह्य शिलासु ते ॥ 39 ॥
गर्तेषु ते मृदं दत्त्वा पूर्यन्ते मुसलैर्भृशम् ॥
बद्धास्तम्भे तथान्यत्र क्षिप्यन्ते सायकैर्नराः ॥ ॥ 40 ॥
शृङ्खलाभिश्च बध्यन्ते लोठ्यन्ते कण्टकेषु च ॥
गन्धेनान्यत्र बोध्यन्ते विषमेण पुनःपुनः ॥ 41 ॥
नारकैश्च तथा सत्त्वैर्नानावेषैर्भयानकैः ॥
यातनाभिश्च बह्वीभिर्याप्यन्ते नरके भृशम् ॥ 42 ॥
अन्योन्यस्य च मांसानि भक्षयन्त्यपरे तथा ॥
हा तात मातेति तथा क्रन्दमानाः पुनःपुनः ॥ 43 ॥
निन्दन्तः स्वानि कर्माणि ताड्यमानाश्च तैर्भटैः ॥
यातनाभिश्च बह्वीभिर्याप्यन्ते भृगु नन्दन ॥ 44 ॥
2.24.m:
And having ground them into flour, others are thoroughly cooked in a pot; / and elsewhere, in iron vessels, with sharp iron stakes,
they are bound by dreadful [demons] on heated [vessels], O mighty-armed one; / and elsewhere, seized, they are dashed against rocks.
Throwing earth over them into pits, they are violently pounded with pestles; / elsewhere men, bound to a post, are shot at with arrows.
They are bound with chains and rolled among thorns; / elsewhere they are roused again and again by a noxious stench.
And by infernal creatures of various terrifying guises / and by many torments they are severely afflicted in hell.
And others devour one another's flesh, / weeping again and again, 'Alas, father! Alas, mother!'
Cursing their own deeds and beaten by those soldiers, / they are made to endure many torments, O son of Bhṛgu.

विमुक्तनारका ह्यन्ये वह्निमन्ये सुशीतलम् ॥
विजानन्ति महाभाग सुखस्पर्शतमं तथा ॥ 45 ॥।
विमुक्तो नारकाच्छीतात्सुखोष्णं हिमसंचयम् ॥
मन्यते सर्वमेवान्यत्सुखस्पर्शतमं तथा ॥ 46 ॥
नरकेभ्यश्च शस्त्रेभ्यो विमुक्तो यो नराधमः ॥
शस्त्राण्यन्यानि जातानि सुखस्पर्शसमानि च ॥47॥
सुखदुःखे तु मानुष्ये त्रिदिवे केवलं सुखम् ॥
नरके दुःखमेवोग्रं सततं भृगुनन्दन ॥ 48॥॥
तृष्णा तत्र क्षुधा तत्र गन्धस्तीव्रो भयङ्करः ॥
यातना विविधाः प्रोक्ता भयं तत्रातिदारुणम् ॥ 49 ॥
दुर्गन्धिकंटकाकीर्णं तथा कुणपसंकुलम् ॥॥
केशास्थिबहुलं भीमं नरकं दुःखमेव तु ॥ 50 ॥
आर्तनादमहानादकाकक्रव्यादसंकुलम् ॥
कृमिकीटपतङ्गाढ्यं पूयासृग्बहुलं तथा ॥ 51 ॥।
2.24.m:
Others, released from infernal fire, perceive another fire / as very cool, O highly fortunate one, and of most pleasant touch.
Released from infernal cold, one considers a mass of snow pleasantly warm, / and everything else as possessing the most pleasant touch.
And that basest of men who is released from the weapons of hell / finds other weapons that strike him to be like pleasant touches.
In human life there are both pleasure and pain, but in heaven only pleasure; / in hell there is only fierce suffering unceasingly, O son of Bhṛgu.
Thirst is there, hunger is there, and an intense, terrifying stench; / manifold torments are proclaimed, and fear there is exceedingly terrible.
Strewn with foul-smelling thorns, crowded with corpses, / filled with hair and bones—dreadful hell is nothing but suffering.
It is filled with cries of distress, loud shrieks, crows, and carnivorous beasts, / teeming with worms, insects, and moths, and full of pus and blood,

कर्मणा केन धर्मज्ञ नरा नरकवासिनः ॥
कां कां योनिं प्रपद्यन्ते तिरश्चो ब्रूहि तन्मम ॥ 1 ॥
पुष्कर उवाच ॥
अमेध्यमध्ये कृमयो महापातकिनो जनाः ॥
भवन्ति बहुधा भूम्यां ततश्चैव शिलासु ते ॥ 2 ॥
तृणगुच्छलतागुल्मद्रुमत्वं प्राप्यते क्रमात् ॥

ब्रह्मस्वहारिणो हिंस्रा रौद्राचाराः सदैव तु ॥
अटव्यां घोररूपायां जायन्ते ब्रह्मराक्षसाः ॥ 4 ॥

कृकलासा हि जायन्ते पिशाचाश्चाप्यनन्तरम् ॥

कृष्णाहयो हि जायन्ते ततः पश्चान्न संशयः ॥ 6 ॥
2.24.m:
Exceedingly frightful are the hells, most terrible, teeming with hosts of frightening venomous serpents; / those who bear devotion to Puruṣottama do not go there, O head of the lineage of Bhṛgu.
2.120 / Rāma said: / By what action, O knower of dharma, do men residing in hell / enter this or that womb of animals? Tell me that.
Puṣkara said: / People who commit great sins become worms in the midst of filth, / in many forms upon the earth, and then within rocks.
Gradually they attain the state of grass, shrubs, creepers, bushes, and trees; / and afterwards they become deer, constantly afflicted by the fear of hunters.
Those who steal the property of a brahmin, being violent and ever cruel in conduct, / are born in a terrible forest as brahmarākṣasas.
Fools devoted to other men's wives are born on parched ground / as chameleons, and immediately thereafter as piśācas; / and after that, without doubt, / they are born as black snakes in the hollow of a withered tree in a terrible forest.

2.24.d:
कूटसाक्षिप्रदाः पापास्त्वमेध्ये कृमयश्चिरम् ॥
कृत्वा भवन्ति सर्पास्ते पिशाचास्तदनन्तरम् ॥ 7 ॥
गुरुमित्रद्रुहः पापा ये च स्वा मिदुहो जनाः ॥
द्विजशिष्यद्रुहश्चैव कृतघ्ना नास्तिकास्तथा ॥ 8 ॥
त्यागिनो बान्धवानां च त्यागिनः शरणार्थिनाम् ॥
निक्षेपहारिणो ये च कन्यकाक्रयिणश्च ये ॥ 9 ॥
अमेध्ये कृमयः सर्पा मृगा व्यालमृगास्तथा ॥
ततो घोरगणोपेता जायन्ते जम्बुकाः खलाः ॥ 10 ॥
परस्वहारिणः पापाः कुञ्जरास्तुरगाः खराः ॥
बलीवर्दास्तथैवोष्ट्रा जायन्ते नात्र संशयः ॥ 11 ॥
हृतं यस्य तु तैर्द्रव्यं तस्य भाग्यानुरूपतः ॥
आत्मदोषानुसारेण जायन्ते धनिनस्तु ते ॥ 12 ॥
चन्द्रार्कग्रहणे भुक्त्वा जायन्ते कुञ्जरा नराः ॥
आमश्राद्धं तथा भुक्त्वा जायन्ते गृध्रयोनिषु ॥13 ॥
असत्प्रतिग्रहं राम गृहीत्वा वानरास्तथा ॥
आशाभङ्गं तथा कृत्वा शृगालाश्च तथाधमाः ॥ 14 ॥
2.24.m:
Sinners who give false testimony become worms in filth for a long time; / having done so, they become snakes, and immediately thereafter piśācas.
Sinful people who betray their gurus and friends, those who betray their master, / those who betray twice-born men and students, the ungrateful, and atheists,
those who abandon their relatives, those who abandon seekers of refuge, / those who embezzle deposits, and those who purchase maidens,
become worms in filth, snakes, deer, and beasts of prey; / then those wicked ones are born as jackals associated with a terrible pack.
Sinners who steal another's property are born as elephants, horses, donkeys, / oxen, and camels; there is no doubt in this.
And according to their own fault, they are born as [beasts of burden for] that wealthy man / whose wealth was stolen by them, in proportion to his fortune.
Men who eat during an eclipse of the moon or the sun are born as elephants; / eating an uncooked śrāddha offering, they are born in the wombs of vultures.
Having accepted improper gifts, O Rāma, [they are born] as monkeys; / and having broken hopes, those base men become jackals.

2.24.d:
सूचकस्तु दुराचारो वागुरिर्नाम जायते ॥
बहु कालं महाभाग भूयोभूय इति श्रुतिः ॥15 ॥
मांसभुग्यावतां राम मांसमश्नाति देहिनाम् ॥
तावतां योनिमाप्नोति भूयोभूयो न संशयः ॥ 16 ॥
भोक्तव्यानि च तैस्तस्य राम मांसान्यसंशयम् ॥
यावन्तः प्राणिनो येन बहिर्वेद्यां निपातिताः॥ 17॥
तावत्यो योनयस्तेन गन्तव्या भृगुसत्तम ॥।
योनौयोनौ च हन्तव्यस्तेनासौ नात्र संशयः ॥ 18॥
वान्ताशी गुणपाशी च पूयभुग्रुधिराशिनः ॥
स्वकर्मविच्युता वर्णा जायन्ते प्रेतयोनिषु॥19॥।
धान्यं हृत्वा भवत्याखुः कांस्यं हंसो जलं प्लवः ॥
मधु दंशः पयः काको रसं श्वा नकुलो घृतम् ॥ 20 ॥
मांसं गृध्रो वसां मद्गुस्तैलं तैलापगः खगः ॥
चीरीवाकस्तु लवणं बलाका शकुनिर्दधि ॥ 21 ॥
2.24.m:
An informer of bad conduct is born as an ensnarer; / for a long time, O highly fortunate one, again and again—so says the scripture.
O Rāma, of as many embodied beings as a meat-eater eats the meat, / into that many wombs he enters again and again; of this there is no doubt.
And his flesh must without doubt be eaten by them, O Rāma; / as many living creatures as are slain by someone outside the sacrificial altar,
to that many wombs he must go, O best of the Bhṛgus, / and in womb after womb he must be killed by that [creature]; there is no doubt in this.
Eaters of vomit, eaters of corpses, eaters of pus, and eaters of blood— / classes that have fallen away from their own duties are born in the wombs of pretas.
Stealing grain, one becomes a mouse; brass, a goose; water, a water-fowl; / honey, a gadfly; milk, a crow; juice, a dog; and ghee, a mongoose.
Stealing meat, [one becomes] a vulture; marrow, a diver-bird; oil, a bird that drinks oil; / salt, a cricket; and curd, a crane or bird of prey.

2.24.d:
कौशेयं तित्तिरिर्हृत्वा क्षौमं हृत्वा च दर्दुरः ॥
कर्पासं तान्तवं क्रौञ्चं गां गोधा वागुदो गुडम् ॥ 22 ॥
छुच्छुन्दरिः शुभान्गन्धान्पत्रशाकं शिखी तथा ॥
मक्षिकास्तु तथैवान्नमकृतान्नं तु शल्यकः ॥ 23 ॥
भेको भवति हृत्त्वाग्निं गृहहारी च तस्करः ॥
रक्तानि हृत्वा वासांसि जायते जीवजीवकः ॥ 24 ॥
वृको मृगेभं व्याघ्राश्वं फलपुष्पं तु मर्कटः ॥।
स्त्रियं हृत्वा भवेद्यक्षो यानमुष्ट्रः पशूनजः ॥ 25 ॥
यद्वा तद्वा परद्रव्यमपहृत्य बलान्नरः ॥
अवश्यं याति तिर्यक्त्वं जग्ध्वा चैवाहुतं हविः ॥ ॥ 26 ॥
तिर्यक्षु दुःखं परमं विदित्वा पापानि वर्ज्यानि नरेण नित्यम् ॥
भक्तिश्च कार्या मधुसूदनस्य तया स दुःखं सकलं जहाति ॥ 27 ॥
2.24.m:
Stealing silk, [one becomes] a partridge; stealing linen, a frog; / cotton fabric, a curlew; a cow, an iguana; and molasses, a bat.
Stealing fine perfumes, [one becomes] a musk-shrew; leafy vegetables, a peacock; / cooked food, a fly; and uncooked food, a porcupine.
Stealing fire, a thief becomes a frog; stealing a house, a gecko; / and stealing red garments, one is born as a jīvañjīvaka bird.
[Stealing] a deer, [one becomes] a wolf; an elephant, a tiger; a horse, a monkey; and fruits and flowers, a monkey; / stealing a woman, one becomes a yakṣa; a vehicle, a camel; and livestock, a goat.
Stealing by force whatever property of another, / or eating an oblation that has not been offered, a man inevitably goes to an animal state.
Knowing that supreme suffering exists among animals, a man must always avoid sins; / and devotion should be offered to Madhusūdana: through it, he abandons all suffering.
